title.zh: 卷一百三十七 列傳第六十二 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟:幼明 幼明子:昕
title.en: Volume 137 Biographies 62: Guo Ziyi and Son: Yao, Son: Xi, Xi's Grandson: Cheng Gu, Son: Ai, Zi's Sons: Zhao, Cong, Xian, Ai's Grandson: Shu, Uncle: You Ming, You Ming's Son: Xin
title.raw: 卷一百三十七 列傳第六十二 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟:幼明 幼明子:昕 Volume 137 Biographies 62: Guo Ziyi and Son: Yao, Son: Xi, Xi's Grandson: Cheng Gu, Son: Ai, Zi's Sons: Zhao, Cong, Xian, Ai's Grandson: Shu, Uncle: You Ming, You Ming's Son: Xin

sentences.zh: 郭子儀子:曜 子:晞 晞孫:承嘏 子:曖 曖子:釗 鏦 銛 曖孫:曙 母弟幼:明 幼明子:昕

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi — sons: Yao; son: Xi; Xi's grandson: Chenggu; son: Ai; Ai's sons: Zhao, Cong, and Xian; Ai's grandson: Shu; uterine younger brother You: Ming; Youming's son: Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's sons included Yao and Xi; Xi's grandson was Chenggu. He also had a son named Ai, whose sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian, and whose grandson was Shu. His younger brother by the same mother was Youming, and Youming's son was Xin.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀，字子儀，華州鄭人。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Zheng in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, styled Ziyi, came from Zheng in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 長七尺二寸。

translations.literal: He stood seven feet two inches in height.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven feet two inches tall.

sentences.zh: 以武舉異等補左衛長史，累遷單于副都護、振遠軍使。

translations.literal: Through the military examination with outstanding rank he was appointed Left Guard Chief Clerk, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Protector-General of the Chanyu Protectorate and Commissioner of the Zhenyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the military examination with the highest honors, he was appointed chief clerk of the Left Guard and later rose through the posts of vice protector-general of the Chanyu Protectorate and commissioner of the Zhenyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，木剌山始築橫塞軍及安北都護府，詔即軍為使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, at Mount Mula the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were first built; an edict appointed him commissioner of that army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Tianbao era (749), construction began at Mount Mula on the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate, and an imperial edict made him commissioner of the new garrison.

sentences.zh: 俄苦地偏不可耕，徙築永清，號天德軍，又以使兼九原太守。

translations.literal: Soon they suffered because the land was remote and could not be farmed; they moved and built at Yongqing, naming it the Tiande Army, and he was also made prefect of Jiuyuan while serving as commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the site proved too remote for farming, so the garrison was relocated to Yongqing and renamed the Tiande Army. Guo Ziyi continued as its commissioner and was also appointed prefect of Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山反，詔子儀為衛尉卿、靈武郡太守，充朔方節度使，率本軍東討。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled; an edict made Ziyi Minister of the Guard and Administrator of Lingwu Commandery, and appointed him Military Commissioner of Shuofang, to lead his army east in punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Tianbao (755), when An Lushan rose in rebellion, Guo Ziyi was named Minister of the Guard and administrator of Lingwu, appointed military commissioner of Shuofang, and ordered to lead his army east against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 子儀收靜邊軍，斬賊將周萬頃，擊高秀岩河曲，敗之，遂收雲中、馬邑，開東陘。

translations.literal: Ziyi recovered the Jingbian Army, beheaded the rebel general Zhou Wanqing, attacked Gao Xiuyan at Hequ and defeated him, then recovered Yunzhong and Mayi and opened the Eastern Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi retook the Jingbian Army, executed the rebel general Zhou Wanqing, routed Gao Xiuyan at Hequ, recovered Yunzhong and Mayi, and reopened the eastern mountain pass.

sentences.zh: 加御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 賊陷常山，河北郡縣皆沒。

translations.literal: The rebels captured Changshan, and the commanderies and counties of Hebei all fell.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels seized Changshan, nearly every commandery and county in Hebei was lost.

sentences.zh: 會李光弼攻賊常山，拔之，子儀引軍下井陘，與光弼合，破賊史思明眾數萬，平幰城。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Guangbi attacked the rebels at Changshan and took it; Ziyi led his army down through Jingxing, joined Guangbi, broke the rebel Shi Siming's force of tens of thousands, and pacified Hancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi meanwhile attacked and captured Changshan. Guo Ziyi marched south through Jingxing, joined forces with him, shattered Shi Siming's army of tens of thousands, and recovered Hancheng.

sentences.zh: 南攻趙郡，禽賊四千，縱之，斬偽守郭獻璆，還常山。

translations.literal: He attacked south into Zhao Commandery, captured four thousand rebels and released them, beheaded the false prefect Guo Xianqiu, and returned to Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Marching south into Zhao Commandery, he took four thousand prisoners and then released them, executed the rebel prefect Guo Xianqiu, and withdrew to Changshan.

sentences.zh: 思明以眾數萬尾軍，及行唐，子儀選騎五百更出挑之。

translations.literal: Siming followed with a force of tens of thousands; when they reached Xingtang, Ziyi selected five hundred horsemen and repeatedly sallied forth to challenge them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming pursued with tens of thousands of men. At Xingtang, Guo Ziyi sent out five hundred picked cavalry in repeated skirmishes to provoke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 三日，賊引去，乘之，又破於沙河，遂趨常陽以守。

translations.literal: After three days the rebels withdrew; he pursued and again defeated them at Shahe, then pressed toward Changyang to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day the rebels pulled back. Guo Ziyi pursued, routed them again at the Sha River, and advanced to hold Changyang.

sentences.zh: 祿山益出精兵佐思明。

translations.literal: Lushan sent out more elite troops to assist Siming.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan dispatched additional crack troops to reinforce Shi Siming.

sentences.zh: 子儀曰：「彼恃加兵，必易我；

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "They rely on their reinforcements and will surely underestimate us;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said, "They are counting on those reinforcements and will take us lightly.

sentences.zh: 易我，心不固，戰則克矣。」

translations.literal: if they underestimate us, their hearts will not be firm, and in battle we can overcome them."
translations.idiomatic: Once they underestimate us, their morale will falter — and then we can defeat them in battle."

sentences.zh: 與戰未決，戮一步將以徇，士殊死鬥，遂破之，斬首二千級，俘五百人，獲馬如之。

translations.literal: They fought without a decision; he executed a foot officer to display as warning, and the soldiers fought with extraordinary desperation, then broke the enemy, beheading two thousand, capturing five hundred men, and taking as many horses.
translations.idiomatic: The battle hung in the balance until he executed a foot officer as an example; his men then fought with desperate fury, broke the enemy line, and killed two thousand, captured five hundred men, and seized an equal number of horses.

sentences.zh: 於是晝揚兵，夜搗壘，賊不得息，氣益老。

translations.literal: Thereupon by day he displayed his troops and by night raided their camps; the rebels could not rest, and their spirit grew ever more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He then paraded his forces by day and raided their camps by night, giving the rebels no rest until their fighting spirit was utterly worn down.

sentences.zh: 乃與光弼、僕固懷恩、渾釋之、陳回光等擊賊嘉山，斬首四萬級，獲人馬萬計。

translations.literal: Then together with Guangbi, Pugu Huai'en, Hun Shizhi, Chen Huiguang, and others he struck the rebels at Jiashan, beheading forty thousand and capturing men and horses by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Joining Li Guangbi, Pugu Huai'en, Hun Shizhi, Chen Huiguang, and others, he attacked the rebels at Jiashan, killing forty thousand and capturing tens of thousands of men and horses.

sentences.zh: 思明跳奔博陵。

translations.literal: Siming fled in haste to Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming fled in disarray to Boling.

sentences.zh: 於是河北諸郡往往斬賊守，迎王師。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the commanderies of Hebei one after another they beheaded rebel garrison commanders and welcomed the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Across Hebei, commanderies one after another executed their rebel governors and welcomed the imperial armies.

sentences.zh: 方北圖范陽，會哥舒翰敗，天子入蜀，太子即位靈武，詔班師。

translations.literal: Just as they were planning a northern campaign against Fanyang, it happened that Geshu Han was defeated, the Son of Heaven entered Shu, the Crown Prince ascended the throne at Lingwu, and an edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: They were preparing a northern drive on Fanyang when news arrived that Geshu Han had been defeated, the emperor had fled into Shu, and the crown prince had been enthroned at Lingwu — whereupon an edict recalled the army.

sentences.zh: 子儀與光弼率步騎五萬赴行在。

translations.literal: Ziyi and Guangbi led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi marched fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to join the court at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷草昧，眾單寡，軍容缺然，及是國威大振。

translations.literal: At that time the court was still in its founding disorder, the forces were few and thin, and military appearance was lacking; with this the nation's prestige greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: The court was still in its infancy, its forces few and its military bearing uncertain — but the arrival of this army restored the empire's prestige in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 拜子儀兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，仍總節度。

translations.literal: Ziyi was appointed Minister of War and Co-Director of the Chancellery under the Secretariat, and still held overall command of the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was appointed minister of war and co-director of the Secretariat, while retaining overall command of the military commission.

sentences.zh: 肅宗大閱六軍，鼓而南，至彭原。

translations.literal: Suzong reviewed the Six Armies on a grand scale, beat the drums and marched south, reaching Pengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong reviewed the Six Armies in full array and marched south to Pengyuan.

sentences.zh: 宰相房琯自請討賊，次陳濤，師敗，眾略盡，故帝唯倚朔方軍為根本。

translations.literal: The Chancellor Fang Guan volunteered to campaign against the rebels; at Chentao the army was defeated and the force was nearly exhausted, so the Emperor relied on the Shuofang Army alone as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Fang Guan volunteered to lead a campaign against the rebels and was routed at Chentao, nearly wiping out his army, the emperor came to rely on the Shuofang forces as his sole foundation.

sentences.zh: 賊將阿史那從禮以同羅、僕骨騎五千，誘河曲九府、六胡州部落數萬迫行在。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ashina Congli with five thousand Tongluo and Pugu cavalry enticed the tribes of the Nine Prefectures and Six Hu States of Hequ, numbering tens of thousands, to press upon the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Ashina Congli, with five thousand Tongluo and Pugu horsemen, incited the tribal peoples of the Nine Prefectures and Six Hu States along the Yellow River bend — tens of thousands strong — to march on the court.

sentences.zh: 子儀以回紇首領葛邏支擊之，執獲數萬，牛羊不可勝計，河曲平。

translations.literal: Ziyi used the Uyghur chieftain Geluozhi to strike them, captured tens of thousands, and cattle and sheep were beyond counting; Hequ was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent the Uyghur chieftain Geluozhi against them, captured tens of thousands of prisoners, and seized untold numbers of cattle and sheep, bringing the Hequ region under control.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，攻賊崔乾祐於潼關，乾祐敗，退保蒲津。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, he attacked the rebel Cui Qianyou at Tong Pass; Qianyou was defeated and withdrew to hold Pu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide era (757), Guo Ziyi attacked the rebel Cui Qianyou at Tong Pass. Cui was defeated and fell back to defend Pu Ford.

sentences.zh: 會永樂尉趙復、河東司戶參軍韓旻、司士徐景及宗室子鋒在城中，謀為內應，子儀攻蒲，復等斬陴者，披闔內軍。

translations.literal: It happened that the Yongle District Defender Zhao Fu, Hedong Registrar Han Min, Commandery Administrator Xu Jing, and a member of the imperial clan named Zifeng were in the city and plotted an inner response; Ziyi attacked Pu, and Fu and the others beheaded the wall guards, opened the gates, and admitted the army.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city, the district defender Zhao Fu, registrar Han Min, administrator Xu Jing, and a royal clansman named Zifeng plotted to open the gates from within. When Guo Ziyi assaulted Pu, they killed the gate guards, threw open the walls, and let the imperial army in.

sentences.zh: 乾祐走安邑，安邑偽納之，兵半入，縣門發，乾祐得脫身走。

translations.literal: Qianyou fled to Anyi; Anyi falsely received him, and when half his troops had entered the county gate closed and Qianyou was able to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qianyou fled to Anyi, where the county feigned welcome — then, once half his force had entered, slammed the gates shut and let him escape with only his life.

sentences.zh: 賊安守忠壁永豐倉，子儀遣子旰與戰，多殺至萬級，旰死於陣。

translations.literal: The rebel An Shouzhong fortified himself at the Yongfeng Granary; Ziyi sent his son Gao to fight, killing many up to ten thousand ranks, and Gao died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel An Shouzhong held the Yongfeng Granary. Guo Ziyi sent his son Gao into battle; though the imperial forces killed as many as ten thousand enemy troops, Gao fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 進收倉。

translations.literal: He advanced and recovered the granary.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi then advanced and captured the granary.

sentences.zh: 於是關、陝始通。

translations.literal: Thereupon the route through Tong and Shaan was first opened.
translations.idiomatic: With that, the route through Tong Pass and Shaan was reopened.

sentences.zh: 詔還鳳翔，進司空，充關內、河東副元帥。

translations.literal: An edict ordered return to Fengxiang; he was promoted to Minister of Works and appointed Vice Commander-in-Chief of Guannei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to Fengxiang, promoted him to minister of works, and named him vice commander-in-chief of Guannei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 率師趨長安，次潏水上。

translations.literal: He led his army toward Chang'an and encamped on the banks of the Yu River.
translations.idiomatic: He led his army toward Chang'an and encamped along the Yu River.

sentences.zh: 賊守忠等軍清渠左。

translations.literal: The rebels Shouzhong and others had their army on the left of the Qing Canal.
translations.idiomatic: An Shouzhong and the other rebel commanders drew up their forces west of the Qing Canal.

sentences.zh: 大戰，王師不利，委仗奔。

translations.literal: In a great battle the imperial army fared ill and cast aside weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the great battle that followed, the imperial army was defeated and fled, abandoning their weapons.

sentences.zh: 子儀收潰卒保武功，待罪於朝，乃授尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Ziyi gathered the routed troops and held Wugong, awaiting punishment at court; he was then appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi rallied the scattered troops and held Wugong, offering himself for punishment at court — yet was instead appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄從元帥廣平王率蕃、漢兵十五萬收長安。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the Commander-in-Chief, the Prince of Guangping, leading one hundred fifty thousand barbarian and Han troops to recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined the Prince of Guangping, supreme commander, in leading a combined force of one hundred fifty thousand tribal and Han troops to retake Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李嗣業為前軍，元帥為中軍，子儀副之，王思禮為後軍，陣香積寺之北，距灃水，臨大川，彌亙一舍。

translations.literal: Li Siye was the vanguard, the Commander-in-Chief the center army with Ziyi as his deputy, and Wang Sili the rearguard; they formed battle lines north of Xiangji Temple, facing the Feng River across a great stream, stretching for one stage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye commanded the vanguard, the prince the center with Guo Ziyi as his deputy, and Wang Sili the rearguard. They drew up north of Xiangji Temple, facing the Feng River across open ground, their battle line stretching a full stage in length.

sentences.zh: 賊李歸仁領勁騎薄戰，官軍囂，嗣業以長刀突出，斬賊數十騎，乃定。

translations.literal: The rebel Li Guiren led crack cavalry in close combat; the imperial army panicked; Siye with long blades burst forth and beheaded several tens of enemy horsemen, and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Li Guiren charged with elite cavalry and threw the imperial line into disorder, Li Siye led a counterattack with long blades, cutting down dozens of horsemen and steadying the army.

sentences.zh: 回紇以奇兵繚賊背，夾攻之，斬首六萬級，生禽二萬，賊帥張通儒夜亡陝郡。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs with surprise troops circled behind the rebels and attacked from both sides; they beheaded sixty thousand, captured twenty thousand alive, and the rebel commander Zhang Tongru fled by night to Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur horsemen swung around the rebel rear in a flanking attack. The imperial forces killed sixty thousand, took twenty thousand prisoners, and the rebel commander Zhang Tongru fled by night toward Shaan.

sentences.zh: 翌日，王入京師，老幼夾道呼曰：「不圖今日復見官軍！」

translations.literal: The next day the Prince entered the capital; old and young lined the roads calling out, "We never imagined we would see the imperial army again today!"
translations.idiomatic: The next day the prince entered the capital. Old and young lined the streets, crying, "We never dreamed we would live to see the imperial army return!"

sentences.zh: 王休士三日，遂東。

translations.literal: The Prince rested the troops for three days, then marched east.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rested his troops for three days, then marched east.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒聞王師至，遣嚴莊悉眾十萬屯陝，助通儒，旌幟鉦鼓徑百餘里。

translations.literal: An Qingxu, hearing the imperial army had arrived, sent Yan Zhuang with his entire force of one hundred thousand to garrison Shaan and aid Tongru; banners, flags, gongs, and drums stretched for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu learned the imperial army was coming, he sent Yan Zhuang with a full force of one hundred thousand to hold Shaan and reinforce Zhang Tongru — their banners, flags, and war drums filling the road for over a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 師至新店，賊已陣，出輕騎，子儀遣二隊逐之，又至，倍以往，皆不及賊營輒反。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xindian the rebels were already in formation; they sent out light cavalry, and Ziyi dispatched two units to pursue; they came again, twice as many as before, and each time before reaching the rebel camp they turned back.
translations.idiomatic: At Xindian the rebels were already in battle order and sent out light cavalry. Guo Ziyi dispatched two squads in pursuit, then sent twice as many again — each time turning back before reaching the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 最後，賊以二百騎掩軍，未戰走，子儀悉軍追，橫貫其營。

translations.literal: Finally the rebels with two hundred horsemen made a surprise attack on the army; without fighting they fled; Ziyi pursued with his entire force and cut straight through their camp.
translations.idiomatic: At last the rebels sent two hundred horsemen in a feint attack, then fled without engaging. Guo Ziyi pursued with his full army and drove straight through the enemy camp.

sentences.zh: 賊張兩翼包之，官軍卻。

translations.literal: The rebels spread both wings to envelop them, and the imperial army fell back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels spread both wings to envelop the imperial force, which fell back.

sentences.zh: 嗣業率回紇從後擊，塵且坌，飛矢射賊，賊驚曰：「回紇至矣！」

translations.literal: Siye led the Uyghurs in a strike from the rear; dust rose thick, flying arrows struck the rebels, and the rebels cried in alarm, "The Uyghurs have come!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye led the Uyghurs in a rear assault; dust billowed skyward as arrows rained on the rebels, who cried in terror, "The Uyghurs are here!"

sentences.zh: 遂大敗，僵屍相屬於道。

translations.literal: Then came a great defeat, and corpses lined the road one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed utterly, and the dead lay heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊等走洛陽，挾慶緒度河保相州，遂收東都。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang and others fled to Luoyang, taking Qingxu across the river to hold Xiang Prefecture, and the Eastern Capital was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang and the others fled to Luoyang, then escorted An Qingxu across the river to hold Xiang Prefecture. The Eastern Capital was recovered.

sentences.zh: 於是河東、河西、河南州縣悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the prefectures and counties of Hedong, Hexi, and Henan were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures and counties of Hedong, Hexi, and Henan were all brought back under imperial control.

sentences.zh: 以功加司徒，封代國公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was additionally made Minister of Education, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to minister of education, enfeoffed as Duke of Dai, and granted a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝遣具軍容迎灞上，勞之曰：「國家再造，卿力也。」

translations.literal: On entering court, the Emperor sent officials in full military dress to welcome him at Bashang and comforted him, saying, "The nation's restoration — it is your strength."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court, the emperor sent officials in full military regalia to welcome him at Bashang and said, "The empire has been restored — and it is your doing."

sentences.zh: 子儀頓首陳謝。

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed his head to the ground and expressed thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi kowtowed and humbly declined the praise.

sentences.zh: 有詔還東都，經略北討。

translations.literal: There was an edict to return to the Eastern Capital and plan the northern punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him back to the Eastern Capital to prepare the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，破賊河上，執安守忠以獻，遂朝京師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, he defeated the rebels on the river and captured An Shouzhong to present him; then he attended court at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianyuan era (758), he defeated the rebels on the Yellow River, captured An Shouzhong, and presented him to the throne before proceeding to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔百官迎于長樂驛，帝禦望春樓待之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to welcome him at Changle Post Station; the Emperor mounted Wangchun Tower to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the entire bureaucracy to welcome him at Changle Post Station and received him personally from Wangchun Tower.

sentences.zh: 進中書令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝即詔大舉九節度師討慶緒，以子儀、光弼皆元功，難相臨攝，第用魚朝恩為觀軍容宣慰使，而不立帥。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately issued an edict a great mobilization of nine military commissioners' armies to campaign against Qingxu; because Ziyi and Guangbi were both founding merit-holders and difficult to place one over the other, they only used Yu Chao'en as Army Supervision and Pacification Commissioner, and did not appoint a supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered a massive campaign against An Qingxu, drawing on the armies of nine military commissioners. Because Guo Ziyi and Li Guangbi were both heroes of the restoration and neither could easily command the other, Yu Chao'en was made army supervision commissioner — but no supreme commander was appointed.

sentences.zh: 子儀自杏園濟河，圍衛州。

translations.literal: Ziyi crossed the river from Xingyuan and besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi crossed the Yellow River from Xingyuan and laid siege to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 慶緒分其眾為三軍。

translations.literal: Qingxu divided his force into three armies.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu divided his force into three armies.

sentences.zh: 將戰，子儀選善射三千士伏壁內，誡曰：「須吾卻，賊必乘壘，若等噪而射。」

translations.literal: About to give battle, Ziyi selected three thousand skilled archers and hid them within the ramparts, instructing them, "Wait until I fall back; the rebels will surely press the walls — then you shout and shoot."
translations.idiomatic: Before the battle, Guo Ziyi picked three thousand expert archers and hid them inside the ramparts with this order: "When I fall back, the rebels will rush the walls — then raise a shout and shoot."

sentences.zh: 既戰，偽遁，賊薄營，伏發，注射如雨。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, he feigned retreat; the rebels pressed the camp; the ambush erupted, and arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, he feigned retreat. The rebels pressed the camp, the ambush sprang, and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 賊震駭，王師整而奮，斬首四萬級，獲鎧胄數十萬，執安慶和，收衛州。

translations.literal: The rebels were shaken with terror; the imperial army reformed and fought fiercely, beheading forty thousand, capturing several hundred thousand sets of armor and helmets, seizing An Qinghe, and recovering Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were thrown into panic. The imperial army reformed and counterattacked, killing forty thousand, seizing hundreds of thousands of sets of armor, capturing An Qinghe, and recovering Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 又戰愁思岡，破之。

translations.literal: He fought again at Chousi Ridge and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Chousi Ridge and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 連營進圍相州，引漳水灌城，漫二時，不能破。

translations.literal: Camp after camp advanced to besiege Xiang Prefecture; they diverted the Zhang River to flood the city for two double-hours, but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies advanced in successive camps to besiege Xiang Prefecture, diverting the Zhang River to flood the city for four hours — yet still could not breach it.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，人相食。

translations.literal: Inside the city grain was exhausted and people ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city food ran out and the starving turned to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 慶緒求救于史思明，思明自魏來，李光弼、王思禮、許叔冀、魯炅前軍遇之，戰鄴南，夷負相當，炅中流矢。

translations.literal: Qingxu sought rescue from Shi Siming; Siming came from Wei; the vanguard of Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong encountered him; they fought south of Ye; casualties on both sides were comparable, and Jiong was struck by a flying arrow.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu appealed to Shi Siming, who marched from Wei. The vanguard under Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong met him south of Ye. The battle was a bloody draw, and Lu Jiong was wounded by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 子儀督後軍，未及戰。

translations.literal: Ziyi directed the rearguard and had not yet joined battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was directing the rearguard and had not yet engaged.

sentences.zh: 會大風拔木，遂晦，跬步不能相物色，於是王師南潰，賊亦走，輜械滿野。

translations.literal: It happened that a great wind uprooted trees and darkness followed; at every step one could not discern another's appearance; thereupon the imperial army broke south, the rebels also fled, and wagons and weapons filled the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Then a gale uprooted trees and plunged the field into darkness so thick that men could not see one another. The imperial army broke and fled south; the rebels fled as well, leaving wagons and weapons strewn across the countryside.

sentences.zh: 諸節度引還。

translations.literal: The various military commissioners led their forces back.
translations.idiomatic: The various military commissioners withdrew their forces.

sentences.zh: 子儀以朔方軍保河陽，斷航橋。

translations.literal: Ziyi with the Shuofang Army held Heyang and severed the pontoon bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi held Heyang with the Shuofang Army and cut the pontoon bridge across the river.

sentences.zh: 時王師眾而無統，進退相顧望，責功不專，是以及於敗。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial army was numerous but without unified command; in advance and retreat they looked to one another; credit for achievement was not concentrated, and thus they came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial forces were numerous but lacked unified command; each unit watched the others in advance and retreat, and with no one bearing sole responsibility for victory, defeat became inevitable.

sentences.zh: 有詔留守東都，俄改東畿、山南東道、河南諸道行營元帥。

translations.literal: There was an edict to remain and garrison the Eastern Capital; soon he was changed to Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Capital Circuit, Shannan East Circuit, and Henan Circuits Field Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left him to garrison the Eastern Capital; soon after he was made commander-in-chief of the field headquarters for the Eastern Capital, Shannan East, and Henan circuits.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩素疾其功，因是媒譖之，故帝召子儀還，更以趙王為天下兵馬元帥，李光弼副之，代子儀領朔方兵。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en had long resented his achievements and on this occasion slandered him through intermediaries; therefore the Emperor recalled Ziyi, replaced him with the Prince of Zhao as Commander-in-Chief of All Armies under Heaven, with Li Guangbi as deputy, to take over Shuofang troops in Ziyi's place.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en had long resented Guo Ziyi's stature and used the defeat to slander him. The emperor recalled Guo Ziyi, named the Prince of Zhao supreme commander of all armies with Li Guangbi as his deputy, and transferred command of the Shuofang forces away from him.

sentences.zh: 子儀雖失軍，無少望，乃心朝廷。

translations.literal: Although Ziyi had lost his army, he harbored no resentment and devoted his heart to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Though stripped of his command, Guo Ziyi showed no bitterness and remained wholly loyal to the throne.

sentences.zh: 思明再陷河、洛，西戎逼擾京輔，天子旰食，乃授邠寧、鄜坊兩節度使，仍留京師。

translations.literal: Siming again captured the He and Luo regions; western barbarians pressed and harassed the capital region; the Son of Heaven ate late; he was then appointed Military Commissioner of both Binning and Fufang, yet still remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming recaptured the He and Luo regions and western tribes harassed the capital, the emperor — eating his meals late with worry — appointed Guo Ziyi military commissioner of Binning and Fufang, yet kept him at court.

sentences.zh: 議者謂子儀有社稷功，而孽寇首鼠，乃置散地，非所宜。

translations.literal: Commentators said Ziyi had merit for the altars of state, yet while the rebel bandits wavered like a mouse at a hole's two ends, he was placed in an idle post — this was not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that a man who had saved the dynasty ought not be sidelined while rebels still lurked — assigning him an inactive post was a mistake.

sentences.zh: 帝亦悟。

translations.literal: The Emperor also came to understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to see they were right.

sentences.zh: 上元初，詔為諸道兵馬都統，以管崇嗣副之，率英武、威遠兵及河西、河東鎮兵，繇邠甯、朔方、大同、橫野軍以趨范陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan, an edict made him Overall Commander of Armies of All Circuits, with Guan Chongsi as deputy, leading the Yingwu and Weiyuan troops and the garrison forces of Hexi and Hedong, by way of Binning, Shuofang, Datong, and Hengye armies to advance on Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shangyuan era, an edict named him overall commander of all circuit armies, with Guan Chongsi as his deputy, to lead the Yingwu and Weiyuan troops plus the garrison forces of Hexi and Hedong through Binning, Shuofang, Datong, and Hengye toward Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 詔下，為朝恩沮解。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Yu Chao'en obstructed and dissolved it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the edict was issued, Yu Chao'en blocked and scuttled the campaign.

sentences.zh: 明年，光弼敗邙山，失河陽。

translations.literal: The next year Guangbi was defeated at Mount Mang and lost Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Li Guangbi was defeated at Mount Mang and lost Heyang.

sentences.zh: 又明年，河中亂，殺李國貞，太原戕鄧景山。

translations.literal: The year after that, Hedong was in turmoil; Li Guozhen was killed, and at Taiyuan Deng Jingshan was slain.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, Hedong erupted in mutiny — Li Guozhen was killed, and in Taiyuan Deng Jingshan was murdered by his own troops.

sentences.zh: 朝廷憂二軍與賊合，而少年新將望輕不可用，遂以子儀為朔方、河中、北庭、潞儀澤沁等州節度行營，兼興平、定國副元帥，進封汾陽郡王，屯絳州。

translations.literal: The court feared the two armies would join the rebels, and young new generals lacked prestige and could not be used; therefore Ziyi was made Field Commissioner of the Military Commissions of Shuofang, Hedong, Beiting, Lu, Yi, Ze, Qin, and other prefectures, and concurrently Vice Commander-in-Chief of Xingping and Dingguo, advanced in enfeoffment to Prince of Fenyang Commandery, and encamped at Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the two mutinous armies might join the rebels, and distrusting the untested young officers available, the court appointed Guo Ziyi field commissioner over Shuofang, Hedong, Beiting, and the Lu-Yi-Ze-Qin region, named him vice commander-in-chief of Xingping and Dingguo, elevated him to Prince of Fenyang, and posted him at Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時帝已不豫，群臣莫有見者，子儀請曰：「老牙受命，將死於外，不見陛下，目不瞑。」

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was already unwell and none of the officials had been granted audience; Ziyi requested, saying, "This old fang accepts the command and will die abroad; if I do not see Your Majesty, my eyes will not close."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already gravely ill and had seen no officials. Guo Ziyi pleaded, "This old soldier accepts his orders knowing he may die in the field — if I cannot see Your Majesty, I shall not close my eyes in death."

sentences.zh: 帝引至臥內，謂曰：「河東事一以委卿。」

translations.literal: The Emperor led him into the inner sleeping chamber and said, "The affairs of Hedong — I entirely entrust them to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received him in his sickroom and said, "All matters in Hedong I entrust entirely to you."

sentences.zh: 子儀嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Ziyi sobbed with tears flowing.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 賜禦馬、銀器、雜彩，別賜絹布九萬。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial horse, silver vessels, and assorted silks; separately he was given ninety thousand bolts of silk and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him an imperial horse, silver vessels, assorted silks, and a separate gift of ninety thousand bolts of silk and cloth.

sentences.zh: 子儀至屯，誅首惡王元振等數十人，太原辛雲京亦治害景山者，諸鎮皆惕息。

translations.literal: When Ziyi reached his encampment, he executed the chief culprits Wang Yuanzhen and several tens of others; at Taiyuan Xin Yunjing also punished those who had harmed Jingshan, and all garrisons trembled and held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post, Guo Ziyi executed the ringleaders, including Wang Yuanzhen, and dozens of their accomplices. At Taiyuan, Xin Yunjing likewise punished those who had killed Deng Jingshan. Every garrison fell silent with fear.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，程元振自謂于帝有功，忌宿將難制，離構百計。

translations.literal: When Daizong ascended, Cheng Yuanzhen considered himself meritorious toward the Emperor, resented that veteran generals were hard to control, and schemed separation by a hundred stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong succeeded to the throne, Cheng Yuanzhen, convinced he had earned the new emperor's gratitude, resented the difficulty of controlling veteran generals and set about dividing them by every means at his disposal.

sentences.zh: 因罷子儀副元帥，加實戶七百，為肅宗山陵使。

translations.literal: Accordingly Ziyi's vice commandership was removed; seven hundred actual households were added to his fief, and he was made Commissioner for Suzong's Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Guo Ziyi of his vice commandership, added seven hundred households to his fief, and assigned him to oversee Emperor Suzong's mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 子儀懼讒且成，盡裒代宗所賜詔敕千餘篇上之，因自明。

translations.literal: Ziyi feared slander would succeed; he gathered all the more than one thousand edicts and orders Daizong had granted him and submitted them upward, thereby making himself clear.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that slander might take hold, Guo Ziyi collected the more than one thousand edicts and orders Emperor Daizong had personally granted him and submitted them all to the throne to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕不德，詒大臣憂，朕甚自愧，自今公毋有疑。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "We lack virtue and have brought worry upon great ministers; We are deeply ashamed; from now on, Duke, harbor no doubts."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Our lack of virtue has caused our great ministers grief — We are deeply ashamed. From this day forward, hold no doubts, Duke."

sentences.zh: 初，帝與子儀平兩京，同天下憂患，至是悔悟，眷禮彌重。

translations.literal: At the beginning the Emperor and Ziyi had pacified the Two Capitals and shared the empire's troubles; at this he repented and understood, and favor and courtesy toward him grew ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and Guo Ziyi had retaken the Two Capitals together and shared the empire's darkest hours; now, moved to remorse, he treated Guo Ziyi with ever greater honor and trust.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義尚盜洛，帝欲使副雍王，率師東討，為朝恩、元振交訾之，乃止。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi still plundered Luoyang; the Emperor wished to have him serve as deputy to the Prince of Yong and lead an army east in punitive campaign, but Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen jointly slandered him, and so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi still held Luoyang by force. The emperor wished to make Guo Ziyi deputy to the Prince of Yong and send him east on campaign, but Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen joined in slandering him, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 會梁崇義據襄州叛，僕固懷恩屯汾州，陰召回紇、吐蕃寇河西，殘涇州，犯奉天、武功，遽拜子儀為關內副元帥，鎮咸陽。

translations.literal: At the same time Liang Chongyi held Xiangzhou in rebellion; Pugu Huai'en encamped at Fenzhou, secretly recalled the Uyghurs and Tibetans to raid Hexi, ravaged Jingzhou, invaded Fengtian and Wugong — and Ziyi was hastily appointed Vice Supreme Commander of Guannei and stationed at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time, Liang Chongyi seized Xiangzhou and rebelled. Pugu Huai'en held Fenzhou and secretly summoned Uyghurs and Tibetans to raid Hexi, laying waste to Jingzhou and threatening Fengtian and Wugong. Guo Ziyi was hurriedly appointed vice supreme commander of Guannei and ordered to hold Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 初，子儀自相州罷歸京師，部曲離散，逮承詔，麾下才數十騎，驅民馬補行隊。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ziyi had been removed from Xiangzhou and returned to the capital, his personal troops had scattered; on receiving the edict, under his command were only several tens of riders, and he forced conscripted civilian horses to fill out his marching column.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guo Ziyi had been recalled from Xiangzhou to the capital, and his personal troops had dispersed. When the edict reached him, he had barely a few dozen horsemen left and had to press civilian horses into service to form a marching column.

sentences.zh: 至咸陽，虜已過渭水，並南山而東，天子跳幸陝。

translations.literal: When he reached Xianyang, the barbarians had already crossed the Wei River and were marching east along the southern slopes of the mountains; the Son of Heaven fled in haste to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Xianyang, the invaders had already crossed the Wei River and were marching east along the southern foothills. The emperor fled in haste to Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞，流涕，董行營還京師。

translations.literal: When Ziyi heard, he wept with tears flowing and personally supervised the march back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, Guo Ziyi wept and personally led his army back toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 遇射生將王獻忠以彀騎叛，劫諸王欲奔虜，子儀讓之，取諸王送行在。

translations.literal: He encountered the archer-cavalry commander Wang Xianzhong, who had rebelled with a band of riders, seized the princes intending to flee to the barbarians; Ziyi rebuked him, took the princes, and sent them to the imperial presence.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the archer-cavalry commander Wang Xianzhong, who had rebelled with a company of horsemen and seized several princes, intent on defecting to the enemy. Guo Ziyi confronted him, recovered the princes, and escorted them to the emperor's temporary court.

sentences.zh: 乃率騎南收兵，得武關防卒及亡士數千，軍浸完。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led cavalry south to gather troops, obtained several thousand garrison soldiers of Wuguan and scattered soldiers, and the army gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his cavalry south to gather reinforcements, mustering several thousand troops from the Wuguan garrison and scattered soldiers, and his army gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 會六軍將張知節迎子儀洛南，大閱兵，屯商州，威震關中。

translations.literal: He met the Six Armies general Zhang Zhijie, who welcomed Ziyi at Luonan; they held a grand review of troops and encamped at Shangzhou, and their authority shook Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies general Zhang Zhijie joined him at Luonan. They held a grand troop review and encamped at Shangzhou, their presence restoring authority throughout Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 乃遣知節率烏崇福、羽林將長孫全緒為前鋒，營韓公堆，擊鼓歡山，張旗幟，夜叢萬炬，以疑賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Zhijie leading Wu Chongfu and the Household Guard general Zhangsun Quanxu as vanguard, encamped at Hanggongdui, beat drums at Huanshan, displayed banners and flags, and at night clustered ten thousand torches to deceive the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Zhijie ahead with Wu Chongfu and the Household Guard general Zhangsun Quanxu as vanguard. They encamped at Hanggongdui, beat drums on Huanshan Hill, raised banners and flags, and at night lit ten thousand torches to confuse the enemy.

sentences.zh: 初，光祿卿殷仲卿募兵藍田，以勁騎先官軍為遊弈，直度滻，民紿虜曰：「郭令公來。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the Director of the Imperial Household Yin Zhongqing had raised troops at Lantian; with strong cavalry he advanced ahead of the regular army as scouting patrols, crossing directly over the Chan River, and the people deceived the barbarians, saying, "Duke Guo has come."
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Director of the Imperial Household Yin Zhongqing had raised troops at Lantian and sent elite cavalry ahead of the main army as scouting patrols, crossing the Chan River directly. Civilians duped the invaders by saying, "Duke Guo has arrived."

sentences.zh: 虜懼。

translations.literal: The barbarians were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders were terrified.

sentences.zh: 會故將軍王甫結俠少，夜鼓硃雀街，呼曰：「王師至！」

translations.literal: At that time the former general Wang Fu gathered bold youths; at night they beat drums on Zhunque Street, crying, "The imperial army has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the former general Wang Fu rallied young men of spirit and at night beat drums along Vermilion Sparrow Street, shouting, "The imperial army is here!"

sentences.zh: 吐蕃夜潰。

translations.literal: The Tibetans fled by night in rout.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Tibetans broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是遣大將李忠義屯苑中，渭北節度使王仲升守朝堂，子儀以中軍繼之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent the great general Li Zhongyi to encamp in the imperial parks, the military commissioner of Weibei Wang Zhongsheng to hold Chaotang, and Ziyi followed with the central army.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi then sent his senior general Li Zhongyi to encamp in the imperial parks, ordered Weibei military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng to hold Chaotang, and followed with the main army.

sentences.zh: 射生將王撫自署京兆尹，亂京城，子儀斬以徇。

translations.literal: The archer-cavalry commander Wang Fu appointed himself Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, threw the capital into disorder, and Ziyi executed him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The archer-cavalry commander Wang Fu had installed himself as metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and was rampaging through the capital. Guo Ziyi had him executed as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 破賊書聞，帝以子儀為京城留守。

translations.literal: News of defeating the rebels was received; the Emperor made Ziyi Garrison Commandant of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When word of the victory reached the emperor, he appointed Guo Ziyi garrison commander of the capital.

sentences.zh: 自變生倉卒，賴子儀復安，故天下皆咎程元振，群臣數論奏。

translations.literal: Since the upheaval arose in sudden haste and thanks to Ziyi the realm was restored to peace, all under Heaven blamed Cheng Yuanzhen, and officials repeatedly presented memorials of discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Because the crisis had erupted so suddenly and Guo Ziyi alone had restored order, the entire realm blamed Cheng Yuanzhen, and officials submitted memorial after memorial against him.

sentences.zh: 元振懼，乃說帝都洛陽，帝可其計。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen was afraid and therefore persuaded the Emperor to move the capital to Luoyang; the Emperor approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his position, Cheng Yuanzhen persuaded the emperor to relocate the capital to Luoyang, and the emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 子儀奏曰：

translations.literal: Ziyi submitted, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 雍州古稱天府，右隴、蜀，左崤、函，襟馮終南、太華之險，背負清渭、濁河之固，地方數千里，帶甲十餘萬，兵強士勇，真用武之國，秦、漢所以成帝業也。

translations.literal: Yong Province was anciently called the Celestial Storehouse; to the right are Long and Shu, to the left Xiao and Han; it clasps the peril of Zhongnan and Taihua, and on its back bears the strength of the clear Wei and muddy rivers; its territory extends several thousand li, with more than one hundred thousand armed men — soldiers strong and warriors brave — truly a state for wielding arms, where Qin and Han achieved imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Province has been called the Celestial Storehouse since antiquity. It holds Long and Shu to the west and the Xiao and Han passes to the east, embraces the natural defenses of Zhongnan and Mount Taihua, and rests against the fortifications of the Wei and Yellow rivers. Its territory spans thousands of li and fields more than a hundred thousand armed men — soldiers fierce and warriors resolute — making it a true martial heartland, the very ground on which the Qin and Han dynasties built their empires.

sentences.zh: 後或處而泰、去而亡者不一姓，故高祖先入關定天下，太宗以來居洛陽者亦鮮。

translations.literal: Later, whether dwelling there brought prosperity or leaving brought extinction was not limited to one surname; therefore Gaozu first entered the Pass to settle the realm, and since Taizong those dwelling at Luoyang have also been few.
translations.idiomatic: Later dynasties prospered or perished depending on whether they held this land — and not one family alone. That is why Emperor Gaozu of Han entered the Pass first to secure the realm, and why, since the time of Emperor Taizong of Tang, few emperors have made their seat at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 先帝興朔方，誅慶緒，陛下席西土，戮朝義，雖天道助順，亦地勢則然。

translations.literal: The late Emperor raised forces at Shuofang and executed Qingxu; Your Majesty took up the western land and executed Chaoyi — though Heaven's Way aided the righteous, the terrain likewise made it so.
translations.idiomatic: Your late father rallied Shuofang and executed An Qingxu; Your Majesty took the western frontier and destroyed Shi Chaoyi. Though Heaven favors the righteous, the geography of the region made such victories possible.

sentences.zh: 比吐蕃馮陵而不能抗者，臣能言其略。

translations.literal: As for how the Tibetans rampaged and could not be resisted — your subject can speak of the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: As for why the Tibetans were able to ravage the land with impunity, I can explain the main reasons.

sentences.zh: 夫六軍皆市井人，竄虛名，逃實賦，一日驅以就戰，有百奔無一前；

translations.literal: The Six Armies are all market-town people who hide behind nominal ranks and evade real levies; drive them into battle in a day and a hundred will flee for every one who advances;
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies are townsmen who bear empty titles and dodge real conscription. Send them into battle overnight and a hundred will flee for every one who advances;

sentences.zh: 又宦豎掩迷，庶政荒奪，遂令陛下彷徨暴露，越在陝服。

translations.literal: Moreover eunuch attendants obstructed and deceived, common government was usurped and abandoned, and thus Your Majesty was left wandering exposed, cast beyond into the lands of Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile eunuchs concealed the truth and usurped government, leaving Your Majesty exposed and wandering, driven as far as Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 斯委任失人，豈秦地非良哉！

translations.literal: This is failure in appointment of men — how could Qin territory not be good!
translations.idiomatic: This was a failure of personnel, not of the land — how could the Qin heartland be unfit!

sentences.zh: 今道路流言，不識信否，鹹謂且都洛陽。

translations.literal: Now rumors on the roads, not knowing whether they are true or false, all say the court will soon make its seat at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors are circulating that the court intends to move the capital to Luoyang — I do not know whether they are true, but everyone is saying so.

sentences.zh: 洛陽自大盜以來，焚埃略盡，百曹榛荒，寰服不滿千戶，井邑如墟，豺狼群嗥；

translations.literal: Luoyang since the Great Bandit has had its ashes and embers nearly exhausted by burning; all offices are overgrown and desolate; within the four quarters households do not reach a thousand; wells and towns are like ruins; wolves and jackals howl in packs;
translations.idiomatic: Since the Great Rebellion, Luoyang has been burned nearly to ashes. Government offices stand overgrown and abandoned; fewer than a thousand households remain in the city, and its streets and marketplaces lie in ruins while wolves howl in packs;

sentences.zh: 東薄鄭、汴，南界徐，北綿懷、衛及相，千里蕭條，亭舍不煙，何以奉萬乘牲餼、供百官次舍哉？

translations.literal: East it adjoins Zheng and Bian, south it borders Xu, north it stretches through Huai, Wei, and Xiang — for a thousand li desolate and empty, relay stations without smoke; how could it supply the sacrificial offerings of the imperial carriage and lodge all officials?
translations.idiomatic: To the east it reaches Zheng and Bian; to the south it borders Xu; to the north it extends through Huai, Wei, and Xiang — a thousand li of desolation with not a wisp of smoke from roadside inns. How could it supply the rites and provisions of the imperial retinue or quarter the entire civil service?

sentences.zh: 且地狹厄，裁數百里，險不足防，適為鬥場。

translations.literal: Moreover the land is narrow and constricted, barely several hundred li; its barriers are insufficient for defense and suited only as a battleground.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the terrain is narrow and confined, barely a few hundred li across, with defenses too weak to hold and better suited as a battlefield.

sentences.zh: 陛下意者不以京畿新罹剽蹂，國用不足乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty's intent stem from the fact that the capital region has newly suffered plunder and ravaging, and state revenues are insufficient?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty perhaps fear that the capital region has been newly ravaged and the treasury cannot bear the cost?

sentences.zh: 昔衛為狄滅，文公廬于曹，衣大布之衣，冠大帛之冠，卒復舊邦，況赫赫天子，躬儉節用，甯為一諸侯下哉？

translations.literal: Formerly when Wei was destroyed by the Di, Duke Wen lodged at Cao, wore garments of coarse cloth and caps of coarse silk, yet in the end recovered his old state — how much more the resplendent Son of Heaven, personally practicing frugality and economizing expenditures — would he consent to rank below a feudal lord?
translations.idiomatic: When the state of Wei was destroyed by the Di tribes, Duke Wen of Wei took refuge in Cao, dressed in coarse hemp and plain silk, and still recovered his kingdom. How much more should an august Son of Heaven, practicing thrift in his own household, refuse to let mere want reduce him below the standing of a feudal lord?

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下斥素餐，去冗食，抑閹寺，任直臣，薄征弛役，恤隱撫鰥，委宰相以簡賢任能，付臣以訓兵禦侮，則中興之功，日月可冀。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to dismiss those who eat without serving, remove redundant consumption, restrain eunuch attendants, employ upright ministers, lighten taxes and relax corvée, show compassion to the distressed and comfort the widowed and alone, entrust the chancellor with selecting the worthy and employing the capable, and assign your subject the task of training troops and repelling insult — then the achievement of revival may be hoped for within days and months.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to purge dead weight from the court, cut redundant expenses, restrain the eunuchs, appoint upright ministers, reduce taxes and corvée labor, show compassion to the suffering and care for widows and orphans, leave the selection of talent to the chancellor, and charge me with training the army and guarding the frontier. Then restoration of the dynasty can be achieved within our lifetime.

sentences.zh: 惟時邁亟還，見宗廟，謁園陵，再造王家，以幸天下。

translations.literal: Only quickly return in season, see the ancestral temples, visit the imperial tombs, restore the House of Tang anew, and thereby bring fortune to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Only hasten Your Majesty's return — pay reverence at the ancestral temples and imperial tombs, restore the Tang house, and bring blessing to the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝得奏，泣謂左右曰：「子儀固社稷臣也，朕西決矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor received the memorial and weeping said to those at hand, "Ziyi is truly a minister of the altars of soil and grain; We have decided on the west."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor wept and said to his attendants, "Guo Ziyi is truly a pillar of the state. I have decided — we stay in the west."

sentences.zh: 乘輿還，子儀頓首請罪，帝勞曰：「用卿晚，故至此。」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned; Ziyi knocked his head and begged forgiveness; the Emperor consoled him, saying, "We employed you too late, and therefore reached this point."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to Chang'an. Guo Ziyi prostrated himself and asked forgiveness. The emperor comforted him, saying, "I relied on you too late — that is why we came to this."

sentences.zh: 乃賜鐵券，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted an iron certificate of immunity and had his likeness painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an iron certificate of immunity and had his portrait placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩縱兵掠並、汾屬縣，帝患之，以子儀兼河東副元帥、河中節度使，鎮河中。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en let his troops plunder subordinate counties of Bing and Fen; the Emperor was troubled and made Ziyi concurrently Vice Supreme Commander of Hedong and military commissioner of Hezhong, stationed at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en's troops were pillaging counties throughout Bing and Fen. Alarmed, the emperor made Guo Ziyi concurrent vice supreme commander of Hedong and military commissioner of Hezhong, with orders to hold the region from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 懷恩子瑒屯榆次，為帳下張惟嶽所殺，傳首京師，持其眾歸子儀。

translations.literal: Huai'en's son Yang encamped at Yuci, was killed by his subordinate Zhang Weiyue, his head sent to the capital, and Zhang led his forces to submit to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's son Yang was encamped at Yuci when he was killed by his subordinate Zhang Weiyue. Zhang sent Yang's head to the capital and led the troops to submit to Guo Ziyi.

sentences.zh: 懷恩懼，委其母走靈州。

translations.literal: Huai'en was afraid, abandoned his mother, and fled to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Huai'en abandoned even his mother and fled to Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，進太尉，兼領北道邠甯、涇原、河西通和吐蕃及朔方招撫觀察使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and concurrently given charge of the northern route as military commissioner and pacification commissioner of Binning, Jingyuan, and Hexi for managing relations with Tibet and of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Guangde era (763), he was promoted to Grand Preceptor and concurrently appointed commissioner for the northern circuit, overseeing Binning, Jingyuan, and Hexi — including relations with Tibet — and pacification commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 辭太尉不拜。

translations.literal: He declined the Grand Preceptor and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post of Grand Preceptor and refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇、党項數十萬入寇，朝廷大恐，詔子儀屯奉天。

translations.literal: Huai'en incited Tibet, Uyghurs, and Tangut peoples numbering several hundreds of thousands to invade; the court was greatly alarmed and ordered Ziyi to encamp at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en persuaded Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, and others — several hundred thousand strong — to invade. The court was terrified and ordered Guo Ziyi to encamp at Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝問計所出，對曰：「無能為也。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked what plan should emerge; he replied, "There is nothing that can be done.
translations.idiomatic: Asked for his counsel, he replied, "There is little we can do by force.

sentences.zh: 懷恩本臣偏將，雖剽果，然素失士心。

translations.literal: Huai'en was originally my deputy general; though fierce and resolute, he has long lost the hearts of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was once my subordinate. He is bold in battle, but he has long since lost the loyalty of his men.

sentences.zh: 今能為亂者，訹思歸之人，劫與俱來，且皆臣故部曲，素以恩信結之，彼忍以刃相向乎？」

translations.literal: Those who can make trouble now are people incited and longing to return home, coerced to come together — and all are my former personal troops, long bound by grace and trust; how could they bear to turn blades against one another?"
translations.idiomatic: The forces he leads are men coerced into rebelling who long only to return home — and they are my former troops, whom I have always treated with loyalty and kindness. Would they truly turn their blades on me?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 虜寇邠州，先驅至奉天，諸將請擊之。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided Binzhou; the vanguard reached Fengtian, and the generals requested to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: The invaders attacked Binzhou, and their vanguard reached Fengtian. The generals urged an immediate attack.

sentences.zh: 子儀曰：「客深入，利速戰。

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "The guests have penetrated deep; they profit from swift battle.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said, "The enemy has marched deep into our territory and wants a quick fight.

sentences.zh: 彼下素德我，吾緩之，當自攜貳。」

translations.literal: Their followers long respect us; if we delay, they will naturally become divided in loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: His troops have long respected me. If we hold back, they will turn against him on their own."

sentences.zh: 因下令：「敢言戰者斬！」

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an order: "Whoever dares speak of battle — behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered, "Anyone who urges battle shall be executed!"

sentences.zh: 堅壁待之，賊果遁。

translations.literal: They held firm behind walls and waited; the rebels indeed fled.
translations.idiomatic: They held their fortifications and waited. The rebels soon withdrew.

sentences.zh: 子儀至自涇陽，恩賚崇縟，進拜尚書令，懇辭，不聽。

translations.literal: Ziyi arrived from Jingyang; favors and gifts were heaped in abundance, and he was promoted and appointed Minister President of the Imperial Secretariat; he earnestly declined but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Jingyang, Guo Ziyi received lavish imperial rewards and was promoted to Minister President of the Imperial Secretariat. He pleaded earnestly to decline but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 詔趣詣省視事，百官往慶，敕射生五百騎執戟寵衛。

translations.literal: An edict urged him to proceed to the ministry and attend to affairs; all officials went to congratulate; an order granted five hundred archer-cavalry with halberds as an honor guard.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded him to take up his duties at the Secretariat. Officials came to offer congratulations, and five hundred archer-cavalry were detailed with halberds as an honor guard.

sentences.zh: 子儀確讓，且言：「太宗嘗踐此官，故累聖曠不置員，皇太子為雍王，定關東，乃得授，渠可猥私老臣，隳大典？

translations.literal: Ziyi firmly declined and moreover said, "Taizong once held this office, therefore successive sages have long left the post vacant; the Crown Prince as Prince of Yong, when he settled Guandong, only then received it — how could one lightly favor an old minister and ruin a great institution?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi refused again, saying, "Emperor Taizong once held this office, and for that reason successive emperors have long kept it vacant. It was granted only to the crown prince as Prince of Yong when he pacified Guandong. How could Your Majesty lightly bestow it on an aging minister and undermine a great precedent?

sentences.zh: 且用兵以來，僭賞者多，至身兼數官，冒進亡恥。

translations.literal: Moreover since the use of arms began, many have received excessive rewards, even holding several offices at once — advancing without shame through presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, excessive rewards have become commonplace, with men holding multiple offices through shameless self-promotion.

sentences.zh: 今凶醜略平，乃作法審官之時，宜從老臣始。」

translations.literal: Now that the wicked are roughly pacified, this is the time to establish law and examine offices — the reform should begin with this old minister."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the rebels are nearly subdued, this is the time to restore proper standards of appointment — and that reform should begin with me."

sentences.zh: 帝不獲已，許之，具所以讓付史官。

translations.literal: The Emperor had no choice and consented; the full text of his declination was entrusted to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly agreed and had Guo Ziyi's refusal recorded in full for the imperial archives.

sentences.zh: 因賜美人六人，從者自副，車服帷帟鹹具。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted six beauties, attendants of his own rank, and chariots, robes, and curtains — all fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: In compensation the emperor granted him six consorts, attendants of corresponding rank, and a full complement of carriages, garments, and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，詔都統河南道節度行營，復鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, an edict made him overall commander of the Henan Circuit military expedition headquarters, and again he was stationed at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yongtai era (765), an edict appointed him overall commander of the Henan circuit expeditionary force, and he resumed his post at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 懷恩盡說吐蕃、回紇、常項、羌、渾、奴剌等三十萬，掠涇、邠，躪鳳翔，入醴泉、奉天，京師大震。

translations.literal: Huai'en persuaded to the full Tibet, Uyghurs, Changxiang, Qiang, Hun, Nula, and others — three hundred thousand — plundered Jing and Bin, trampled Fengxiang, entered Liquan and Fengtian; the capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en mustered Tibetans, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qiang, Hun, Nula, and other peoples — three hundred thousand in all — who ravaged Jing and Bin, swept through Fengxiang, and pushed into Liquan and Fengtian. The capital was shaken with terror.

sentences.zh: 於是帝命李忠臣屯渭橋，李光進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝廷玉屯便橋，駱奉先、李日越屯厔盩，李抱玉屯鳳翔，周智光屯同州，杜冕屯坊州，天子自將屯苑中。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor ordered Li Zhongchen to encamp at Weiqiao, Li Guangjin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bianqiao, Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue at Zhouzhi, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang, Zhou Zhiguang at Tongzhou, Du Mian at Fangzhou; the Son of Heaven personally led troops and encamped in the imperial parks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deployed his forces across the region: Li Zhongchen at Weiqiao, Li Guangjin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bianqiao, Luo Fengxian and Li Riyue at Zhouzhi, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang, Zhou Zhiguang at Tongzhou, and Du Mian at Fangzhou — while the emperor himself took command in the imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 急召子儀屯涇陽，軍才萬人。

translations.literal: He urgently summoned Ziyi to encamp at Jingyang; the army numbered only ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi was urgently recalled to Jingyang — his force numbered barely ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 比到，虜騎圍已合，乃使李國臣、高升、魏楚玉、陳回光、硃元琮各當一面，身自率鎧騎二千出入陣中。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, barbarian cavalry had already closed the encirclement; he thereupon had Li Guochen, Gao Sheng, Wei Chuyu, Chen Huiguang, and Zhu Yuancong each hold one face, while he personally led two thousand armored cavalry in and out of the battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived, the enemy cavalry had already encircled him. He assigned Li Guochen, Gao Sheng, Wei Chuyu, Chen Huiguang, and Zhu Yuancong each to one sector while he personally led two thousand armored horsemen through the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 回紇怪問，：「是謂誰？」

translations.literal: The Uyghurs asked in surprise: "Who is that?"
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs asked in astonishment: "Who is that?"

sentences.zh: 報曰：「郭令公。」

translations.literal: They were answered, "Duke Guo."
translations.idiomatic: They were told, "Duke Guo."

sentences.zh: 驚曰：「令公存乎？

translations.literal: In alarm they said, "Does Duke Guo still live?
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, they cried, "Is Duke Guo still alive?

sentences.zh: 懷恩言天可汗棄天下，令公即世，中國無主，故我從以來。

translations.literal: Huai'en said the Heavenly Qaghan had abandoned the realm, Duke Guo had passed away, China had no ruler — therefore we followed and came.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en told us the Heavenly Qaghan had abandoned the realm, Duke Guo was dead, and China had no master — that is why we came.

sentences.zh: 公今存，天可汗存乎？」

translations.literal: You are alive now — does the Heavenly Qaghan still live?"
translations.idiomatic: If you are alive, does the Heavenly Qaghan live as well?"

sentences.zh: 報曰：「天子萬壽。」

translations.literal: They were answered, "The Son of Heaven enjoys ten thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: They were told, "The Son of Heaven is alive and well."

sentences.zh: 回紇悟曰：「彼欺我乎！」

translations.literal: The Uyghurs understood and said, "Was he deceiving us!"
translations.idiomatic: Realizing they had been deceived, the Uyghurs cried, "He lied to us!"

sentences.zh: 子儀使諭虜曰：「昔回紇涉萬里，戡大憝，助復二京，我與若等休戚同之。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent someone to address the barbarians, saying, "Formerly the Uyghurs crossed ten thousand li, crushed the great rebel, and helped recover the Two Capitals — I share weal and woe with you all.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent an envoy to address them: "Once the Uyghurs marched ten thousand li to crush the great rebel and help retake the Two Capitals. You and I shared life and death together.

sentences.zh: 今乃棄舊好，助叛臣，一何愚！

translations.literal: Now you abandon the old friendship and aid a rebel minister — how exceedingly foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Now you throw away that bond to aid a rebel — how foolish!

sentences.zh: 彼背主棄親，于回紇何有？」

translations.literal: He betrayed his lord and abandoned kin — what concern is he to the Uyghurs?"
translations.idiomatic: He betrayed his sovereign and abandoned his own kin — what does he owe the Uyghurs?"

sentences.zh: 回紇曰：「本謂公雲亡，不然，何以至此。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs said, "We originally thought the Duke was dead — otherwise, how would we have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs replied, "We believed Duke Guo was dead. Otherwise, how could we have come to this?

sentences.zh: 今誠存，我得見乎？」

translations.literal: Now if he truly lives, may we see him?"
translations.idiomatic: If he truly lives, may we see him?"

sentences.zh: 子儀將出，左右諫：「戎狄野心不可信。」

translations.literal: Ziyi was about to go out; those at his side remonstrated, "Barbarians have wild hearts and cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi prepared to go out in person. His attendants warned, "The barbarians are treacherous by nature and cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 子儀曰：「虜眾數十倍，今力不敵，吾將示以至誠。」

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "The barbarian host is several tens of times our strength; now our power cannot match theirs — I will show utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said, "They outnumber us tenfold. We cannot fight them — I must show them my good faith in person."

sentences.zh: 左右請以騎五百從，又不聽。

translations.literal: Those at his side requested five hundred cavalry to accompany him; again he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When his attendants offered five hundred cavalry as an escort, he refused again.

sentences.zh: 即傳呼曰：「令公來！」

translations.literal: Immediately the call went out: "The Duke is coming!"
translations.idiomatic: He called out, "The Duke is coming!"

sentences.zh: 虜皆持滿待。

translations.literal: The barbarians all nocked full and waited.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ranks stood with bows fully drawn.

sentences.zh: 子儀以數十騎出，免胄見其大酋曰：「諸君同艱難久矣，何忽亡忠誼而至是邪？」

translations.literal: Ziyi with several tens of riders went out, removed his helm and saw their great chieftain, saying, "You gentlemen have shared hardship for so long — why suddenly abandon loyalty and righteousness and come to this?"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi rode out with a few dozen horsemen, removed his helmet, and faced the Uyghur chieftains: "We have shared hardship for so long — why have you suddenly abandoned loyalty and come to this?"

sentences.zh: 回紇舍兵下馬拜曰：「果吾父也。」

translations.literal: The Uyghurs set aside their weapons, dismounted, and bowed, saying, "He is indeed our father."
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs lowered their weapons, dismounted, and bowed: "It truly is our father."

sentences.zh: 子儀即召與飲，遺錦彩結歡，誓好如初。

translations.literal: Ziyi immediately summoned them to drink, bestowed silks to cement friendship, and swore amity as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi invited them to drink, presented them with brocades as tokens of friendship, and renewed their alliance as before.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「吐蕃本吾舅甥國，無負而來，棄親也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he said, "Tibet is originally our uncle-nephew state; they came without provocation on our part — they have abandoned kinship.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Tibet is bound to us by ties of marriage and kinship. They came here without cause — they have betrayed family bonds.

sentences.zh: 馬牛被數百里，公等若倒戈乘之，若俯取一芥，是謂天賜，不可失。

translations.literal: Horses and cattle cover several hundred li; if you gentlemen turn your blades and strike them, it will be like stooping to pick a mustard seed — this is Heaven's gift and cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Their horses and cattle stretch for hundreds of li. If you turn your swords against them, the spoils will be yours for the taking — a gift from Heaven that must not be missed.

sentences.zh: 且逐戎得利，與我繼好，不兩善乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, drive out the barbarians and gain profit, while continuing friendship with me — is this not doubly good?"
translations.idiomatic: Drive off the Tibetans for gain, keep your friendship with me — would that not serve us both?"

sentences.zh: 會懷恩暴死，群虜無所統一，遂許諾。

translations.literal: At that time Huai'en died suddenly; the various barbarians had none to unify them, and they thereupon agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Huai'en died suddenly. With no leader to hold the alliance together, the Uyghurs agreed.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃疑之，夜引去。

translations.literal: Tibet grew suspicious and withdrew by night.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious, the Tibetans withdrew under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 子儀遣將白元光合回紇眾追躡，大軍繼之，破吐蕃十萬於靈台西原，斬級五萬，俘萬人，盡得所掠士女牛羊馬橐駝不勝計。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent the general Bai Yuanguang to join with the Uyghur host in pursuit; the great army followed, and at Lingtai's western plain broke Tibet's hundred thousand, beheading fifty thousand levels, capturing ten thousand, and fully recovering the plundered men and women, cattle, sheep, horses, and camels beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi sent general Bai Yuanguang with the Uyghur forces in pursuit, followed by the main army. At the western plain of Lingtai they smashed a hundred thousand Tibetans, killing fifty thousand, taking ten thousand prisoners, and recovering untold numbers of captive men and women, cattle, sheep, horses, and camels.

sentences.zh: 遂自涇陽來朝，加實封二百戶，還河中。

translations.literal: Thereupon from Jingyang he came to court; two hundred actual households were added to his fief, and he returned to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled from Jingyang to court, received an additional two hundred households added to his fief, and returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 大曆元年，華州節度使周智光謀叛，帝間道以蠟書賜子儀，令悉軍討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dali, the Huazhou military commissioner Zhou Zhiguang plotted rebellion; the Emperor by secret route sent a wax-sealed letter bestowing it on Ziyi, ordering him to lead all his troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Dali era (766), Huazhou military commissioner Zhou Zhiguang plotted rebellion. The emperor sent a sealed dispatch by secret courier ordering Guo Ziyi to march with his entire army against him.

sentences.zh: 同、華將吏聞軍起，殺智光，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: The officers of Tong and Hua heard the army was raised, killed Zhiguang, and sent his head to beneath the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the officers of Tong and Hua learned that an army was marching, they killed Zhiguang and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年，吐蕃寇涇州，詔移屯涇陽。

translations.literal: In the second year, Tibet raided Jingzhou; an edict ordered relocation to encamp at Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Tibet attacked Jingzhou, an edict ordered Guo Ziyi to move his encampment to Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 邀戰於靈州，敗之，斬首二萬級。

translations.literal: He offered battle at Lingzhou, defeated them, and beheaded twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He offered battle at Lingzhou, routed the enemy, and took twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，還河中。

translations.literal: The next year, he returned to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃復寇靈武，詔率師五萬屯奉天，白元光破虜于靈武。

translations.literal: Tibet again raided Lingwu; an edict ordered him to lead fifty thousand troops to encamp at Fengtian; Bai Yuanguang defeated the barbarians at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet attacked Lingwu again, an edict ordered him to lead fifty thousand troops to Fengtian while Bai Yuanguang defeated the invaders at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 議者以吐蕃數為盜，馬璘孤軍在邠不能支，乃以子儀兼邠甯慶節度使，屯邠州，徙璘為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: Discussants, because Tibet repeatedly acted as bandits and Ma Lin's isolated army at Bin could not sustain itself, made Ziyi concurrently military commissioner of Binning-Qing and stationed him at Binzhou, transferring Lin to be military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tibet kept raiding and Ma Lin's isolated force at Bin could not hold the line, the court made Guo Ziyi concurrent military commissioner of Binning-Qing, stationed at Binzhou, and transferred Ma Lin to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 回紇赤心請市馬萬匹，有司以財乏，止市千匹。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Chixin requested to purchase ten thousand horses; the relevant offices, citing lack of funds, permitted only the purchase of one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur chieftain Chixin requested to purchase ten thousand horses from the court. The ministry, citing insufficient funds, authorized only one thousand.

sentences.zh: 子儀曰：「回紇有大功，宜答其意，中原須馬，臣請內一歲奉，佐馬直。」

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "The Uyghurs have great merit; we should respond to their wish; the central plain needs horses — your subject requests to contribute one year's salary to assist with the horse price."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi said, "The Uyghurs rendered great service to the dynasty. We ought to honor their request. The heartland needs horses — I offer to contribute one year's salary toward the purchase."

sentences.zh: 詔不聽，人許其忠。

translations.literal: The edict did not accept; people praised his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The edict declined his offer, but people praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 九年，入朝，對延英，帝與語吐蕃方強，慷慨至流涕。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he came to court, audience in Yanying; the Emperor spoke with him of Tibet's present strength, and with such fervor that tears flowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year (779) he came to court for an audience in the Yanying Hall. When the emperor spoke of Tibet's growing power, Guo Ziyi grew so moved that tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 退，上書曰：

translations.literal: On retiring, he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing, he submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 朔方，國北門，西禦犬戎，北虞獫狁，五城相去三千里。

translations.literal: Shuofang is the realm's northern gate, defending west against the Rong dogs, guarding north against Xianyun; five fortresses stand three thousand li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang is the empire's northern gate — guarding the west against the frontier Rong and the north against the Xianyun. Its five garrison cities stand three thousand li apart.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中，戰士十萬，馬三萬匹，僅支一隅。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, warriors numbered one hundred thousand, horses thirty thousand — barely sustaining one corner.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, it fielded a hundred thousand soldiers and thirty thousand horses — and that force could barely hold one sector.

sentences.zh: 自先帝受命靈武，戰士從陛下征討無甯歲。

translations.literal: Since the Former Emperor received the Mandate at Lingwu, warriors have followed Your Majesty on campaigns without a year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since the late emperor received the Mandate at Lingwu, the soldiers have followed Your Majesty on campaign year after year without respite.

sentences.zh: 頃以懷恩亂，痍傷雕耗，亡三分之二，比天寶中止十之一。

translations.literal: Recently, because of Huai'en's rebellion, wounds and depletion — two-thirds lost; compared with Tianbao, barely one in ten remains.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's rebellion recently left the armies wounded and depleted. Two-thirds have perished, leaving barely one-tenth of the Tianbao strength.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃兼吞河、隴，雜羌、渾之眾，歲深入畿郊，勢逾十倍，與之角勝，豈易得邪？

translations.literal: Now Tibet has swallowed Hexi and Longyou and mixed Qiang and Hun hosts; each year they thrust deep into the capital precincts — strength exceeds tenfold; to contest victory with them, how easily obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Now Tibet has swallowed Hexi and Longyou and mustered Qiang and Hun peoples. Each year they thrust deep into the capital region, and their strength exceeds ours tenfold. How easily could victory be won against them?

sentences.zh: 屬者虜來，稱四節度，將別萬人，人兼數馬。

translations.literal: When the barbarians came lately, they claimed four military commissioners, each leading ten thousand separately; every man had several horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the invaders came recently, they fielded four separate expeditionary commands, each with ten thousand men — and every soldier rode several horses.

sentences.zh: 臣所統士不當賊四之一，馬不當賊百之二，外畏內懼，將何以安？
