translations.literal: The soldiers under your subject's command are not equal to one-fourth of the rebels'; horses not equal to two in a hundred of theirs — fearing without and within, how shall we be secure?
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers under my command are less than a quarter of the enemy's, and our horses less than two in a hundred of theirs. Fearing them without and within, how can we be secure?

sentences.zh: 臣惟陛下制勝，力非不足，但簡練不至，進退未一，時淹師老，地廣勢分。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Your Majesty's power to prevail is not insufficient — but drilling has not reached adequacy, advance and retreat are not unified, time delays weary the troops, the land is broad and forces scattered.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty's power to prevail is not insufficient — but training has fallen short, advance and retreat are not coordinated, delays have worn the troops down, and the territory is so broad that our forces are scattered.

sentences.zh: 願于諸道料精卒滿五萬者，列屯北邊，則制勝可必。

translations.literal: I wish that from the various circuits picked elite troops reaching fifty thousand be arrayed and encamped on the northern frontier — then prevailing can be assured.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that fifty thousand picked troops be drawn from the circuits and posted along the northern frontier — then victory can be assured.

sentences.zh: 竊惟河南、河北、江淮大鎮數萬，小者數千，殫屈稟給，未始搜擇。

translations.literal: I privately consider that the great garrisons of Henan, Hebei, and Jianghuai number tens of thousands, the smaller several thousands — exhausting tribute supplies, yet never has there been selection.
translations.idiomatic: The great garrisons of Henan, Hebei, and Jianghuai field tens of thousands of men each, the smaller ones several thousands — exhausting the supplies sent to them, yet no one has ever selected the best from among them.

sentences.zh: 臣請追赴關中，勒步隊，示金鼓，則攻必破，守必全，長久之策也。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that they be summoned to Guanzhong, drilled as infantry columns, displayed with gongs and drums — then attack will surely break the foe, defense surely hold complete: a lasting strategy.
translations.idiomatic: I request that they be summoned to Guanzhong, drilled as infantry columns, and marshaled with drums and bells — then attack will surely break the enemy and defense will surely hold. That is the lasting strategy.

sentences.zh: 又自陳衰老，乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He also declared himself aged and weary and requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He also declared his age and weariness and asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕終始倚賴，未可以去位。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "From first to last I rely upon you; you cannot leave your post."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "From first to last I rely upon you. You cannot leave your post."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，詔還朝，攝塚宰，充山陵使，賜號「尚父」，進位太尉、中書令，增實封通前二千戶，給糧千五百人，芻馬二百匹，盡罷所領使及帥。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, an edict ordered return to court; he acted as chief mourner, served as director of the imperial tomb, was granted the title "Imperial Father," promoted to Grand Preceptor and Zhongshu Ling, actual fief increased to two thousand households including prior grants, granted rations for fifteen hundred, two hundred fodder horses — all his commissioner and command posts were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, an edict summoned Guo Ziyi back to court. He served as chief mourner and director of the imperial tomb, was granted the title "Imperial Father," and was promoted to Grand Preceptor and Minister President of the Imperial Secretariat. His actual fief was increased by two thousand households, bringing the total to two thousand; he received rations for fifteen hundred men and two hundred fodder horses. All the commissioner and command posts he had held were abolished.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，疾病，帝遣舒王到第傳詔省問，子儀不能興，叩頭謝恩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, he fell ill; the Emperor sent the Prince of Shu to his residence to convey an edict of inquiry; Ziyi could not rise, kowtowed in thanks for the grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianzhong era (781), he fell ill. The emperor sent the Prince of Shu to his residence with an edict of inquiry. Guo Ziyi could not rise from his bed and kowtowed in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十五。

translations.literal: He passed away, age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 帝悼痛，廢朝五日。

translations.literal: The Emperor grieved in pain and suspended court for five days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for five days.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣往吊，隨喪所須，皆取於官。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to attend mourning; whatever the funeral required was taken from the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the officials to attend the mourning rites. Everything the funeral required was supplied from the state.

sentences.zh: 贈太師。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 陪葬建陵。

translations.literal: Buried alongside the Jian Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried alongside the Jian Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 及葬，帝禦安福門，哭過其喪，百官陪位流涕。

translations.literal: At the burial, the Emperor attended at Anfu Gate, wept passing the funeral procession; officials accompanying in place shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: At the burial the emperor attended at Anfu Gate, weeping as the procession passed. The officials standing in attendance wept as well.

sentences.zh: 賜諡曰忠武，配饗代宗廟廷。

translations.literal: Posthumous name granted: Zhongwu; enshrined in sacrifice at Emperor Daizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the posthumous name Zhongwu and enshrined for sacrifice in Emperor Daizong's temple.

sentences.zh: 著令，一品墳崇丈八尺，詔特增丈，以表元功。

translations.literal: Regulations set a first-rank tomb mound at one zhang and eight chi; an edict specially added one zhang to mark extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations fixed the tomb mound of a first-rank official at one zhang and eight chi. An edict specially added another zhang to honor his extraordinary service.

sentences.zh: 子儀事上誠，禦下恕，賞罰必信。

translations.literal: Ziyi served the sovereign with sincerity, commanded subordinates with forbearance; rewards and punishments were trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi served the sovereign with sincerity and commanded his subordinates with forbearance. His rewards and punishments were always trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 遭幸臣程元振、魚朝恩短毀，方時多虞，握兵處外，然詔至，即日就道，無纖介顧望，故讒間不行。

translations.literal: He suffered slander from favored ministers Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en; though the times held many anxieties and he held troops abroad, when an edict arrived he set out the same day without the slightest hesitation — therefore slanderous schemes could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Favored ministers Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en slandered him. Though the times were perilous and he held troops far from court, whenever an edict arrived he set out the same day without the slightest hesitation. For that reason their slanders never took hold.

sentences.zh: 破吐蕃靈州，而朝恩使人發其父墓，盜未得。

translations.literal: After defeating Tibet at Lingzhou, Chao'en sent men to open his father's tomb; no treasure was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: After he defeated the Tibetans at Lingzhou, Yu Chao'en sent men to open his father's tomb, but they found no treasure.

sentences.zh: 子儀自涇陽來朝，中外懼有變，及入見，帝唁之，即號泣曰：「臣久主兵，不能禁士殘人之墓，人今發先臣墓，此天譴，非人患也。」

translations.literal: Ziyi came from Jingyang to court; within and without feared trouble; on entering audience the Emperor condoled him; he immediately wailed and said, "Your subject long commanded troops and could not forbid soldiers from despoiling others' tombs; now others have opened my forebear's tomb — this is Heaven's punishment, not human malice."
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi came to court from Jingyang, court and country alike feared trouble. On his audience the emperor offered condolences, and he immediately wailed: "I long commanded troops and could not keep my soldiers from despoiling others' tombs. Now others have opened my father's tomb — this is Heaven's punishment, not human malice."

sentences.zh: 朝恩又嘗約子儀修具，元載使人告以軍容將不利公。

translations.literal: Chao'en also once invited Ziyi to a banquet; Yuan Zai sent someone to inform that the army inspector intended harm to the Duke.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en once invited Guo Ziyi to a banquet. Yuan Zai sent word that the army inspector intended him harm.

sentences.zh: 其下衷甲願從，子儀不聽，但以家僮十數往。

translations.literal: His subordinates wore armor beneath their robes wishing to accompany; Ziyi would not listen, taking only a dozen household servants.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates wore armor under their robes and wished to accompany him. Guo Ziyi refused and went with only a dozen household servants.

sentences.zh: 朝恩曰：「何車騎之寡？」

translations.literal: Chao'en said, "Why so few carriages and riders?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en asked, "Why so few carriages and riders?"

sentences.zh: 告以所聞。

translations.literal: He told what he had heard.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chao'en what he had heard.

sentences.zh: 朝恩泣曰：「非公長者，得無致疑乎？」

translations.literal: Chao'en wept and said, "If not for your magnanimity as an elder, would I not have been suspected?"
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en wept and said, "Had you not been so magnanimous, would I not have been suspected?"

sentences.zh: 田承嗣傲狠不軌，子儀嘗遣使至魏，承嗣西望拜，指其膝謂使者曰：「茲膝不屈於人久矣，今為公拜。」

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi was arrogant, fierce, and unruly; Ziyi once sent an envoy to Wei; Chengsi bowed facing west, pointed to his knees, and told the envoy, "These knees have not bent to anyone for long — today I bow for you."
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi was arrogant and unruly. Guo Ziyi once sent an envoy to Wei. Chengsi bowed facing west, pointed to his knees, and told the envoy, "These knees have not bent to anyone for a long time — today I bow for you."

sentences.zh: 李靈耀據汴州，公私財賦一皆遏絕，子儀封幣道其境，莫敢留，令持兵衛送。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao held Bianzhou and blocked all public and private revenue; Ziyi's sealed tribute passed through his territory — none dared detain it; he ordered armed escort to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao held Bianzhou and blocked all public and private revenue. When Guo Ziyi's sealed tribute passed through his territory, no one dared detain it — he ordered armed escorts to see it through.

sentences.zh: 麾下宿將數十，皆王侯貴重，子儀頤指進退，若部曲然。

translations.literal: Under his command were several tens of veteran generals, all nobles of high rank; Ziyi commanded their advance and retreat with a gesture, as if personal retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen veteran generals under his command were nobles of the highest rank, yet Guo Ziyi directed their advance and retreat with a gesture, as though they were his personal retainers.

sentences.zh: 幕府六十餘人，後皆為將相顯官，其取士得才類如此。

translations.literal: Over sixty men in his staff office — later all became generals, chief ministers, and distinguished officials; such was his talent in recruiting men.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty men served in his staff office, and later all became generals, chief ministers, or other distinguished officials. Such was his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 與李光弼齊名，而寬厚得人過之。

translations.literal: Equal in fame with Li Guangbi, yet in magnanimity winning hearts he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He was equal in fame to Li Guangbi, but surpassed him in the magnanimity that wins men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 子儀歲入官俸無慮二十四萬緡。

translations.literal: Ziyi's annual official salary was no less than two hundred forty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's annual official salary amounted to no less than two hundred forty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 宅居親仁裏四分之一，中通永巷，家人三千相出入，不知其居。

translations.literal: His residence occupied a quarter of Qinren Ward; a central lane ran through it; three thousand household members came and went — visitors did not know where he lived.
translations.idiomatic: His residence occupied a quarter of Qinren Ward, with a central lane running through it. Three thousand household members came and went, and visitors could not tell where he actually lived.

sentences.zh: 前後賜良田、美器、名園、甲館不勝紀。

translations.literal: Successive grants of fine lands, beautiful vessels, famous gardens, and grand mansions beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years he received fine lands, beautiful vessels, famous gardens, and grand mansions beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 代宗不名，呼為大臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong did not speak his name, calling him "Great Minister."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong never spoke his name, addressing him only as "Great Minister."

sentences.zh: 以身為天下安危者二十年，校中書令考二十四。

translations.literal: For twenty years he embodied the realm's safety and peril; assessed as Zhongshu Ling twenty-four times.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years he embodied the safety and peril of the realm, and received twenty-four annual performance reviews as Minister President of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 八子七婿，皆貴顯朝廷。

translations.literal: Eight sons and seven sons-in-law — all distinguished and prominent at court.
translations.idiomatic: His eight sons and seven sons-in-law all rose to distinction at court.

sentences.zh: 諸孫數十，不能盡識，至問安，但頷之而已。

translations.literal: Several tens of grandsons — he could not know them all; when they came to greet him, he merely nodded.
translations.idiomatic: He had several dozen grandsons and could not know them all. When they came to greet him, he merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 富貴壽考，哀榮終始，人臣之道無缺焉。

translations.literal: Wealth, honor, long life, glory in mourning from start to finish — as a minister, nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth, honor, long life, and glory from beginning to end — as a minister, nothing was wanting in his career.

sentences.zh: 子曜、旰、晞、昢、晤、曖、曙、映，而四子以才顯。

translations.literal: Sons Yao, Gan, Xi, Pan, Wu, Ai, Shu, and Ying — among them four sons were distinguished by talent.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yao, Gan, Xi, Pan, Wu, Ai, Shu, and Ying. Four of them distinguished themselves by talent.

sentences.zh: 子 曜

translations.literal: Son: Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜，性沉靜，資貌瑰傑。

translations.literal: Yao — nature sedate and quiet, endowment and appearance splendid and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was sedate by nature, with a splendid and commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 累從節度府辟署，破虜有功，為開陽府果毅都尉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs; defeated barbarians with merit; made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly recruited to military commissioner staffs, won merit defeating the enemy, and was made Guoyi Commander of Kaiyang District.

sentences.zh: 至德初，推子儀功，授衛尉卿，累進太子詹事、太原郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide, in recognition of Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia; promoted in succession to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhide era (756), in recognition of Guo Ziyi's merit, he was appointed Guardian of the Imperial Insignia and was later promoted to Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince's Household and Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 子儀專征伐，曜留治家事，少長無閑言。

translations.literal: Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns; Yao remained to manage household affairs — among young and old, no idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: While Guo Ziyi devoted himself to campaigns, Yao remained at home to manage the household — and among the family, young and old alike, there was no gossip.

sentences.zh: 諸弟或飾池館，盛車服，曜獨以朴簡自處。

translations.literal: Some of his brothers ornamented pools and halls, lavish in carriages and robes; Yao alone lived in plain simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his brothers ornamented their pools and halls and went about in lavish carriages and robes. Yao alone lived plainly.

sentences.zh: 子儀罷兵，遷太子少保，昆弟六人，共制拜官。

translations.literal: When Ziyi laid down arms, Yao was transferred to Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; six brothers jointly regulated official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi laid down his arms, Yao was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince. The six brothers jointly regulated official appointments within the family.

sentences.zh: 子儀薨，以遺命簿上四朝所賜名馬珍物，德宗復賜之，乃悉散諸弟。

translations.literal: When Ziyi passed away, per his will the register listed famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns; Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed all to his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi died, his will listed the famous horses and treasures granted by four reigns. Emperor Dezong re-granted them, and Yao distributed everything among his brothers.

sentences.zh: 居喪以禮，疾甚，或勸茹蔥薤，終不屬口。

translations.literal: He observed mourning according to rites; very ill, some urged leeks and chives — he never let them touch his lips.
translations.idiomatic: He observed mourning rites properly. When he grew very ill, some urged him to eat leeks and chives, but he never let them touch his lips.

sentences.zh: 後盧杞秉政，忌勳族，子儀婿太僕卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰皆以次得罪。

translations.literal: Later Lu Qi held power, jealous of meritorious clans; Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Lu Qi held power, he was jealous of meritorious clans. Guo Ziyi's sons-in-law — Grand Master of Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Assistant Director of the Palace Stores Li Dongqing, and Director of the Imperial Household Wang Zai — were punished one after another.

sentences.zh: 奸人幸其危，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜大恐，獨宰相張鎰力保護。

translations.literal: Villains preyed on their peril and seized many estates and slaves; Yao was greatly afraid — only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Villains preyed on the family's peril and seized many estates and slaves. Yao was greatly afraid, and only Chief Minister Zhang Huan forcefully protected him.

sentences.zh: 德宗稍聞之，詔有司曰：「尚父子儀有大勳力，保乂王家，嘗誓山河，琢金石，許宥十世。

translations.literal: Dezong gradually heard of it and issued an edict the offices, saying, "Imperial Father Ziyi had great merit, preserved and governed the royal house, once sworn on mountains and rivers, carved in metal and stone, granted exemption for ten generations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong gradually learned of this, he issued an edict to the offices: "Imperial Father Guo Ziyi rendered great service and preserved the imperial house. An oath sworn on mountains and rivers and carved in metal and stone granted his line exemption for ten generations.

sentences.zh: 前日其家市田宅奴婢，而無賴者以尚父歿，妄論奪之，自今有司毋得受。」

translations.literal: The other day his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing the Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them — from now on the offices shall not accept such claims."
translations.idiomatic: Recently his family purchased estates and slaves, yet rogues, citing Imperial Father's death, falsely seized them. From now on the offices shall not accept such claims."

sentences.zh: 建中三年，卒，贈太子太傅，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianzhong he died; posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince; posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianzhong era (782) he died. He was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince and granted the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 初，曜襲代國公，食二千戶。

translations.literal: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Yao inherited the title Duke of Dai, with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，詔減半以封晞、曖、映、曙，人二百五十戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan, an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu — two hundred fifty households each.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era (785), an edict halved the fief to enfeoff Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu with two hundred fifty households each.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復詔四人各減五十戶，封曜子鋒、晤子鐇各百戶雲。

translations.literal: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, another edict reduced each of the four by fifty households and enfeoffed Yao's son Feng and Wu's son Zheng with one hundred households each.

sentences.zh: 子 晞

translations.literal: Son: Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Xi.

sentences.zh: 晞，善騎射，從征伐有功，復兩京，戰最力，出奇兵破賊，累進鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Xi — skilled in riding and archery; followed campaigns with merit; in recovering the Two Capitals fought with greatest force; with surprise troops broke the rebels; promoted in succession to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was skilled in riding and archery. He followed the campaigns with merit, fought with the greatest force in recovering the Two Capitals, and broke the rebels with surprise attacks. He was promoted in succession to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 河中軍亂，子儀召首惡誅之，其支黨猶反仄，晞選親兵晝夜警，以備非常，奸人不得發。

translations.literal: When the Hezhong army mutinied, Ziyi summoned the ringleaders and executed them; their followers still restive — Xi selected personal troops to stand guard day and night against the unexpected, so villains could not act.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hezhong army mutinied, Guo Ziyi summoned the ringleaders and executed them, but their followers remained restless. Xi selected personal troops to stand guard day and night against trouble, so villains could not act.

sentences.zh: 以功拜殿中監。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was appointed Palace Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃、回紇入寇，加御史中丞，領朔方軍援邠州，與馬璘合軍擊虜，破之。

translations.literal: When Tibet and the Uyghurs invaded, he was added as Vice Censor-in-Chief, led the Shuofang army to aid Binzhou, joined forces with Ma Lin to strike the barbarians, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet and the Uyghurs invaded, he was made Vice Censor-in-Chief, led the Shuofang army to relieve Binzhou, joined forces with Ma Lin to strike the enemy, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 虜復來，陣涇水北，子儀遣晞率徒兵五千、騎五百襲虜。

translations.literal: The barbarians came again, arrayed north of the Jing River; Ziyi sent Xi to lead five thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came again and arrayed north of the Jing River, Guo Ziyi sent Xi with five thousand infantry and five hundred cavalry to attack them.

sentences.zh: 晞以兵寡不進，須暮，賊半濟，乃擊，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Xi, with few troops, did not advance; he waited until dusk; when the rebels were half across the river, he struck and beheaded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: With too few troops to attack at once, Xi held back until dusk. When the enemy were half across the river, he struck and took five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 加御史大夫，子儀固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chief Censor; Ziyi firmly declined on his behalf, and the appointment stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Chief Censor, but Guo Ziyi firmly declined on his behalf, and the appointment went no further.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，值硃泚亂，南走山谷。

translations.literal: While observing mourning for his father, the Zhu Ci rebellion broke out; he fled south into the mountains and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father, the Zhu Ci rebellion broke out. He fled south into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊舁致之，欲汙以官，佯暗不答；

translations.literal: The rebels carried him off, wishing to defile him with office; he feigned stupidity and gave no answer;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels carried him off and tried to force an office on him. He feigned stupidity and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 賊露兵脅之，不動。

translations.literal: the rebels displayed weapons to threaten him — he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels displayed weapons to threaten him, he did not stir.

sentences.zh: 數以城中事貽書李晟。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he sent letters to Li Sheng with news of affairs in the city.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly sent letters to Li Sheng with intelligence about affairs in the city.

sentences.zh: 既而奔奉天。

translations.literal: Before long he fled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 天子還，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned, he was changed to Companion to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Xi was made Companion to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 子鋼，從朔方杜希全幕府。

translations.literal: His son Gang served on the staff of Du Xiquan of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang served on the staff of Du Xiquan in Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 希全檄為豐州刺史，晞憐其弱不任事，丐罷。

translations.literal: Xiquan ordered by dispatch that Gang be Prefect of Fengzhou; Xi, pitying his weakness as unfit for office, begged that the appointment be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Xiquan ordered Gang appointed Prefect of Fengzhou. Xi, pitying his son's weakness as unfit for the post, begged that the appointment be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣使者召鋼，鋼疑得罪，挺身走吐蕃，不納。

translations.literal: Dezong sent a messenger to summon Gang; Gang suspected guilt, fled bodily to Tibet — they would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong sent a messenger to summon Gang. Gang suspected he was being punished and fled to Tibet, which refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 希全執送京師，賜死。

translations.literal: Xiquan arrested him and sent him to the capital; death was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xiquan arrested him and sent him to the capital, where he was granted death.

sentences.zh: 晞坐免，尋復太子賓客。

translations.literal: Xi was demoted for responsibility; before long restored as Companion to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was demoted for his son's offense but was soon restored as Companion to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 累封趙國公。

translations.literal: Accumulated enfeoffments to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 孫承嘏。

translations.literal: Grandson: Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 晞孫 承嘏

translations.literal: Xi's grandson: Chenggu.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's grandson: Chenggu.

sentences.zh: 承嘏，字復卿，幼秀異，通《五經》。

translations.literal: Chenggu, style Fuching — brilliant and unusual in youth, mastered the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggu, style Fuching, was brilliant as a youth and mastered the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 元和中，及進士第，累遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, he passed the jinshi examination; promoted in succession to Attendant of Daily Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and was promoted in succession to Attendant of Daily Affairs.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，以孝聞。

translations.literal: While mourning his mother, he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother, he was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，為諫議大夫，言政事得失。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe, he became Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master and spoke on the gains and losses of government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Taihe era (832) he became Remonstrance and Policy Grand Master and spoke on the rights and wrongs of government policy.

sentences.zh: 文宗以鄭注為太僕卿，承嘏極論其非，注頗懼。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong made Zheng Zhu Grand Master of Imperial Stud; Chenggu argued strongly against it; Zhu was quite afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong appointed Zheng Zhu Grand Master of Imperial Stud, Chenggu argued strongly against it, and Zhu was quite alarmed.

sentences.zh: 進給事中。

translations.literal: Promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 俄出為華州刺史，給事中盧載還詔書，且言：「承嘏數封駁稱職，宜在禁闥。」

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as Prefect of Huazhou; Supervising Censor Lu Zai returned the edict and moreover said, "Chenggu has repeatedly memorialized and remonstrated competently — he ought to remain in the inner court."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Prefect of Huazhou. Supervising Censor Lu Zai returned the edict and said, "Chenggu has repeatedly memorialized and remonstrated with competence. He ought to remain in the inner court."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕謂久次，欲優其稍入耳。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "I thought he had long served and wished to favor him slightly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I thought he had served long enough and wished to favor him with a slight promotion."

sentences.zh: 乃復留給事中。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was retained as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore retained as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時江淮旱，用度不支，詔宰相分領度支、戶部。

translations.literal: At the time Jianghuai suffered drought; expenses could not be met; an edict ordered the chief ministers to divide supervision of the Revenue and Census bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jianghuai was stricken by drought and expenses could not be met. An edict ordered the chief ministers to divide supervision of the Revenue and Census bureaus.

sentences.zh: 承嘏言：「宰相調和陰陽，安黎庶。

translations.literal: Chenggu said, "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang and secure the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggu said, "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang and secure the common people.

sentences.zh: 若使閱視簿書，校緡帛，非所宜。」

translations.literal: If made to examine ledgers and check silk and cash, that is not what is fitting."
translations.idiomatic: It is not fitting for them to pore over ledgers and audit silk and cash."

sentences.zh: 帝順納。

translations.literal: The Emperor readily accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor readily accepted this.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗稱其儒素，無貴驕氣，不類勳家。

translations.literal: The Emperor once praised his scholarly plainness, without noble-arrogant air — not like a meritorious house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised his scholarly plainness and lack of aristocratic arrogance — not at all like the scion of a great military house.

sentences.zh: 每進對，恩接備厚。

translations.literal: Whenever he came forward for audience, favor and reception were fully generous.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came forward for audience, the emperor received him with the fullest favor.

sentences.zh: 方大任用，會卒。

translations.literal: Just as he was to be greatly entrusted, he happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was on the verge of great preferment, he died.

sentences.zh: 家無餘貲，親友為辦喪祭。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus funds; relatives and friends provided funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: His household had no surplus wealth, and relatives and friends provided for his funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Posthumously gifted Minister of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 子 曖

translations.literal: Son · Ai
translations.idiomatic: His son Ai

sentences.zh: 曖，字曖，乙太常主簿尚昇平公主。

translations.literal: Ai, courtesy name Ai, while Principal Recorder of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, married Princess Shengping.
translations.idiomatic: Ai, whose courtesy name was also Ai, married Princess Shengping while serving as Principal Recorder of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 曖年與公主侔，十餘歲許昏。

translations.literal: Ai's years matched the Princess; marriage was agreed when both were little over ten.
translations.idiomatic: Ai and the princess were the same age; betrothal was arranged when both were barely in their teens.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，試殿中監，封清源縣侯，寵冠戚裏。

translations.literal: Invested as Commandant Escort, probationary Director of the Palace Directorate, enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan — favor crowned the imperial affines.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commandant Escort, given probationary rank as Director of the Palace Directorate, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan — the favorite among all imperial affines.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the end of Dali, made Supervisory Commissioner as Left Regular Mounted Companion.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Dali era (766–779), he was appointed Supervisory Commissioner as Left Regular Mounted Companion.

sentences.zh: 建中時，主坐事，留禁中。

translations.literal: During Jianzhong, the Princess was implicated in an affair and detained in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianzhong era (780–783), the princess was implicated in a case and confined to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 硃泚亂，逼署曖官，辭以居喪被疾。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's rebellion — forced appointment of Ai to office; he declined on grounds of mourning and illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, the rebels pressed him to accept office, but he declined on the grounds that he was in mourning and ill.

sentences.zh: 既而與公主奔奉天。

translations.literal: Then he fled with the Princess to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He then fled with the princess to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，釋主罪，進曖金紫光祿大夫，賜實封五十戶。

translations.literal: Dezong commended this, released the Princess's guilt, advanced Ai to Golden Purple-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, bestowed substantive fief of fifty households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong commended him, absolved the princess of guilt, promoted Ai to Golden Purple-Gleaming Grand Master of the Palace, and granted him a substantive fief of fifty households.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，襲代國公。

translations.literal: Third year of Zhenyuan, inherited Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenyuan (787) he inherited the title Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十八，贈尚書左僕射，初，曖女為廣陵郡王妃。

translations.literal: Died, age forty-eight; posthumously gifted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Earlier, Ai's daughter was consort to the Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight and was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs. Earlier, Ai's daughter had been consort to the Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 王即位，是為憲宗。

translations.literal: The Prince ascended — this is Xianzong.
translations.idiomatic: When that prince ascended the throne, he became Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 妃生穆宗。

translations.literal: The consort bore Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: The consort bore Muzong.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，尊妃為皇太后，贈曖太傅。

translations.literal: Muzong established, honored the consort as Empress Dowager, posthumously gifted Ai as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, the consort was honored as Empress Dowager, and Ai was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 四子：鑄、釗、鏦、銛。

translations.literal: Four sons: Zhu, Zhao, Cong, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Zhu, Zhao, Cong, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 鑄襲封。

translations.literal: Zhu inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu inherited the noble title.

sentences.zh: 曖子 釗

translations.literal: Ai's son · Zhao
translations.idiomatic: Ai's son Zhao

sentences.zh: 釗，長七尺，方口豐下。

translations.literal: Zhao, height seven chi, square mouth, full lower face.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao stood seven chi tall, with a square mouth and full jaw.

sentences.zh: 代宗朝，以外孫為奉禮郎。

translations.literal: During Daizong's reign, as grandson by a daughter, made Master of Ceremonial Offerings.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Daizong's reign, as the emperor's grandson by a daughter, he was made Master of Ceremonial Offerings.

sentences.zh: 累官至左金吾大將軍，改檢校工部尚書，為邠甯節度使，入為司農卿。

translations.literal: Accumulated to Left General of the Golden Gallant Army, changed to Supervisory Commissioner as Minister of Works, made Bianning Military Commissioner, entered court as Grand Minister of Farming.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left General of the Golden Gallant Army, was appointed Supervisory Commissioner as Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of Bianning, and then entered court as Grand Minister of Farming.

sentences.zh: 憲宗寢疾，宦豎或妄議廢立者。

translations.literal: Xianzong bedridden with illness; eunuch attendants sometimes recklessly discussed deposing and establishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong lay bedridden with illness, eunuch attendants sometimes recklessly discussed deposing and replacing the heir.

sentences.zh: 穆宗問計於釗，答曰：「殿下為太子，當旦夕視膳，何外慮乎？」

translations.literal: Muzong asked Zhao for counsel; he replied, "Your Highness as Heir Apparent ought morning and evening to attend to the imperial meals — what outside worries?"
translations.idiomatic: Muzong asked Zhao for counsel. Zhao replied, "Your Highness, as heir apparent, should attend to the emperor's meals morning and evening — why fret over outside matters?"

sentences.zh: 時稱得元舅體。

translations.literal: At the time called having attained the manner of the chief maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people said he had the bearing of a proper chief maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，檢校戶部尚書兼司農卿。

translations.literal: Muzong ascended; Supervisory Commissioner as Minister of Revenue, concurrently Grand Minister of Farming.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended the throne, Zhao was appointed Supervisory Commissioner as Minister of Revenue, concurrently serving as Grand Minister of Farming.

sentences.zh: 俄為河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: Soon made Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Military Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 徙河中尹，領晉絳慈隰節度。

translations.literal: Transferred as Prefect of the Capital of Hedong, holding Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Li military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Hedong and took command of the Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Li prefectures.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，召拜兵部尚書，又帥劍南東川。

translations.literal: Jingzong established, summoned and invested Minister of War, also commanded Eastern Chuan of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, Zhao was summoned and appointed Minister of War, and also commanded Eastern Chuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 太和中，南蠻寇蜀，取成都外郛，杜元穎不能禦，詔釗兼領西川節度。

translations.literal: During Taihe, southern barbarians raided Shu, took Chengdu's outer wall; Du Yuanying could not repel; edict ordered Zhao to additionally hold Western Chuan military commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, southern tribes raided Shu and took Chengdu's outer wall. Du Yuanying could not repel them, and an edict ordered Zhao to take additional command of Western Chuan.

sentences.zh: 未行，蠻眾已略梓州。

translations.literal: Before he departed, the barbarian host had already overrun Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the tribal forces had already overrun Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 州兵寡，不可用。

translations.literal: The prefectural soldiers were few, unusable.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural troops were too few to be of use.

sentences.zh: 釗貽書譙蠻首帟巔以侵叛意。

translations.literal: Zhao sent a letter reproaching the barbarian chieftain Zhidian for intentions of invasion and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao sent a letter reproaching the tribal chieftain Zhidian for invading and rebelling.

sentences.zh: 帟巔曰：「元穎不自守，數侵吾圉，我以是報。」

translations.literal: Zhidian said, "Yuanying would not hold his own, repeatedly encroaching on our borders — I repay thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zhidian replied, "Yuanying failed to hold his own posts and repeatedly encroached on our territory — I am merely repaying him in kind."

sentences.zh: 乃與修好，約無相犯。

translations.literal: Thereupon made peace, agreed not to violate each other.
translations.idiomatic: A peace was then concluded with a pact of mutual non-aggression.

sentences.zh: 天子嘉之，即拜西川節度使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven commended this, immediately invested Western Chuan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended this and immediately appointed him Military Commissioner of Western Chuan.

sentences.zh: 以疾請代，為太常卿，卒，贈司徒。

translations.literal: Because of illness requested replacement; made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; died; posthumously gifted Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He later requested relief due to illness, was made Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and died. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 子仲文、仲恭、仲詞。

translations.literal: Sons Zhongwen, Zhonggong, Zhongci.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhongwen, Zhonggong, and Zhongci.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，詔仲文襲太原郡公。

translations.literal: Second year of Kaicheng, edict ordered Zhongwen inherit Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng (837), an edict ordered Zhongwen to inherit the title Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 給事中盧弘宣奏：「劍妻沈，公主女，代宗皇帝外孫，其子仲詞尚饒陽公主。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Lu Hongxuan memorialized: "Zhao's wife Shen, a princess's daughter, Emperor Daizong's granddaughter by a daughter; her son Zhongci married Princess Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Lu Hongxuan memorialized: "Zhao's wife Shen was the daughter of a princess and Emperor Daizong's granddaughter by a daughter. Her son Zhongci married Princess Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 仲文冒嫡不應襲。

translations.literal: Zhongwen falsely claimed legitimacy as heir — ought not inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen falsely claimed to be the legitimate heir and ought not inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 使仲文承嫡，則沈當黜，且仲詞亦不得尚主。」

translations.literal: If Zhongwen were made to succeed as legitimate heir, then Shen would have to be dismissed, and moreover Zhongci also could not marry a princess."
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongwen were allowed to succeed as legitimate heir, Shen would have to be set aside, and Zhongci would also lose his right to marry a princess."

sentences.zh: 乃詔仲詞檢校殿中少監、駙馬都尉，襲封。

translations.literal: Thereupon edict made Zhongci Supervisory Commissioner as Vice Director of the Palace Directorate, Commandant Escort, inherit enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon appointed Zhongci Supervisory Commissioner as Vice Director of the Palace Directorate and Commandant Escort, and granted him the inherited title.

sentences.zh: 而仲文乙太皇太后故，置不問。

translations.literal: But on account of the Grand Empress Dowager, left uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: But on account of the Grand Empress Dowager, the authorities let the matter rest.

sentences.zh: 仲恭曆詹事府丞，亦尚金堂公主。

translations.literal: Zhonggong served as Assistant Director of the Heir Apparent's Household, also married Princess Jintang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonggong served as Assistant Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and also married Princess Jintang.

sentences.zh: 曖子 鏦

translations.literal: Ai's son · Cong
translations.idiomatic: Ai's son Cong

sentences.zh: 鏦，字利用，尚德陽郡主。

translations.literal: Cong, courtesy name Liyong, married the Princess of Deyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, courtesy name Liyong, married the Princess of Deyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 詔裴延齡為主營第長興裏。

translations.literal: Edict ordered Pei Yanling to build a mansion for the Princess in Changxing Ward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Pei Yanling to build the princess a mansion in Changxing Ward.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，主進封漢陽公主，擢鏦檢校國子祭酒、駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Shunzong established, Princess advanced to Princess of Hanyang; promoted Cong Supervisory Commissioner as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education, Commandant Escort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shunzong took the throne, the princess was promoted to Princess of Hanyang, and Cong was promoted to Supervisory Commissioner as Chancellor of the Directorate of Education and Commandant Escort.

sentences.zh: 自景龍後，外戚多為檢校官，不治事。

translations.literal: Since Jinglong, affines by marriage were mostly Supervisory Commissioners — did not administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jinglong era, imperial affines had mostly held supervisory posts without actually administering affairs.

sentences.zh: 宰相薦其才，不當以外戚廢，乃拜右金吾將軍，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Chief ministers recommended his talent — ought not be discarded for being an affine; thereupon invested Right Golden Gallant General, enfeoffed Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers recommended his ability and argued he should not be sidelined merely for being an imperial affine. He was therefore appointed Right General of the Golden Gallant Army and enfeoffed as Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 恭遜折節，不以富貴加人。

translations.literal: Respectful and yielding, restraining himself — did not impose on people by wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Humble and unassuming, he did not lord his wealth and rank over others.

sentences.zh: 性周畏，不立赫赫名。

translations.literal: By nature circumspect and cautious — did not establish a blazing reputation.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was circumspect and cautious and sought no blazing reputation.

sentences.zh: 有諫於上，退必毀稿，家人子弟無知者。

translations.literal: When remonstrating before the sovereign, on retiring always destroyed the draft — family members and sons had no knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When he remonstrated with the emperor, he always destroyed his draft on returning home, so that even family and household knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 別墅在都南，尤勝塏，穆宗嘗幸之，置酒極歡。

translations.literal: Country villa south of the capital, especially fine terrain — Muzong once visited, set out wine in utmost merriment.
translations.idiomatic: His country villa south of the capital stood on especially fine land. Emperor Muzong once visited it and feasted there in great delight.

sentences.zh: 改太子詹事，充閑廄宮苑使。

translations.literal: Changed to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, filled the post of Commissioner of the Privy Paddocks and Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Commissioner of the Privy Paddocks and Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously gifted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously enfeoffed as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 曖子 銛

translations.literal: Ai's son · Xian
translations.idiomatic: Ai's son Xian

sentences.zh: 銛，性和易，累為殿中監，尚西河公主。

translations.literal: Xian, nature mild and easy, repeatedly served as Director of the Palace Directorate, married Princess Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was mild and easygoing by nature, served repeatedly as Director of the Palace Directorate, and married Princess Xihe.

sentences.zh: 鏦卒，代為太子詹事、宮苑閑廄使。

translations.literal: Cong died; replaced him as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Privy Paddocks.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong died, Xian succeeded him as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Commissioner of the Palace Parks and Privy Paddocks.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，暴卒。

translations.literal: Third year of Changqing, sudden death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changqing (823) he died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 太后遣使按問發疾狀，久乃解。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager dispatched envoys to investigate the circumstances of his sudden illness — only after long time was it resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sent envoys to investigate the circumstances of his sudden death, and the inquiry was not resolved for some time.

sentences.zh: 初，西河主降沈氏，生一子，銛無嗣，以沈氏子嗣。

translations.literal: Initially, Princess Xihe had married down to the Shen clan and borne one son; Xian had no heir — made Shen clan's son successor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Princess Xihe had married a commoner of the Shen clan and borne a son. Xian had no heir of his own, so he adopted the Shen clan's son as his successor.

sentences.zh: 曖孫 曙

translations.literal: Ai's grandson · Shu
translations.idiomatic: Ai's grandson Shu

sentences.zh: 曙，代宗朝累官司農卿。

translations.literal: Shu, during Daizong's reign repeatedly served up to Grand Minister of Farming.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, during Emperor Daizong's reign, rose through several posts to Grand Minister of Farming.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，曙方領家兵獵苑北，聞蹕至，伏謁道左，遂從乘輿入駱穀。

translations.literal: Dezong visited Fengtian; Shu was just leading household troops hunting north of the park — hearing the imperial procession arrive, prostrated himself at the roadside, then followed the imperial carriage into Luogu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Shu was hunting north of the imperial park with his household troops. Hearing the imperial procession approach, he prostrated himself by the roadside and then escorted the emperor's carriage into Luogu Valley.

sentences.zh: 霖雨塗潦，衛兵或異語。

translations.literal: Continuous rain made roads muddy; guard soldiers sometimes spoke oddly.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains had turned the roads to mire, and some of the guard soldiers murmured dissent.

sentences.zh: 帝召謂曰：「朕不德而苦公等，宜執朕送硃泚，以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Emperor summoned and said, "I lack virtue and have implicated you all — you ought seize me and deliver me to Zhu Ci, to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned them and said, "I have been without virtue and have brought hardship upon you all. You ought to seize me and deliver me to Zhu Ci to answer before the realm."

sentences.zh: 諸將皆感泣曰：「願死生從陛下。」

translations.literal: All generals wept movedly and said, "We wish to follow Your Majesty in life and death."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wept and said, "We wish to follow Your Majesty in life and death."

sentences.zh: 時曙與功臣子李昇、韋清、令狐建、李彥輔被甲請見，言曰：「南行路險，且虞奸變。

translations.literal: At the time Shu with meritorious ministers' sons Li Sheng, Wei Qing, Linghu Jian, Li Yanfu — armored, requested audience, saying, "Southward the road is perilous, and we fear treacherous revolt.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shu, together with the sons of meritorious ministers — Li Sheng, Wei Qing, Linghu Jian, and Li Yanfu — came in armor to request an audience. They said, "The road south is perilous, and we fear treachery along the way.

sentences.zh: 臣等世蒙恩，今相誓，願更挾帝馬。」

translations.literal: We your subjects generation upon generation received grace; now mutually sworn — wish further to escort the imperial horse."
translations.idiomatic: We have received the dynasty's grace for generations. We have sworn together that we wish to ride alongside and guard Your Majesty's mount."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted their request.

sentences.zh: 帝還，曙、清擢金吾大將軍，餘並為禁軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor returned; Shu and Qing promoted to Grand Generals of the Golden Gallant Army; the rest all made Guard Army generals.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, Shu and Qing were promoted to Grand Generals of the Golden Gallant Army, and the rest were all made generals of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 曙終祁國公。

translations.literal: Shu ended as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shu ultimately held the title Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 子儀母弟幼明，性謹願無過，拙于武，喜賓客。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's younger brother by the same mother Youming — nature cautious and obedient without fault, clumsy at martial arts, fond of guests.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's younger uterine brother Youming was cautious and unassuming, free of fault, inept at martial affairs, and fond of entertaining guests.

sentences.zh: 以子儀故，終少府監，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: Because of Ziyi, ended as Director of the Palace Workshops, posthumously gifted Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Through Guo Ziyi's influence he rose to Director of the Palace Workshops and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 子昕，肅宗末為四鎮留後。

translations.literal: Son Xin, at end of Suzong's reign was Rear Commissioner of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin, at the end of Emperor Suzong's reign, served as Rear Commissioner of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 關、隴陷，不得歸，朝廷但命官遙領其使。

translations.literal: Guan and Long fell — could not return; court only assigned officials to hold the commission from afar.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongguan and Longyou fell, he could not return, and the court could only appoint officials to hold his commission at a distance.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，昕始與伊西、北庭節度使曹令忠遣使入朝。

translations.literal: Second year of Jianzhong, Xin first with Yi-West and Beiting Military Commissioner Cao Lingzhong dispatched envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong (781), Xin and Cao Lingzhong, Military Commissioner of Yi-West and Beiting, at last sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 德宗詔曰：「四鎮、二庭，統西夏五十七蕃十姓部落，國朝以來，相與率職。

translations.literal: Dezong's edict said, "Four Garrisons and Two Courts govern the Western Regions' fifty-seven tribes and ten surnames — since the dynasty, mutually leading duties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong's edict read: "The Four Garrisons and Two Courts govern fifty-seven tribal peoples and ten surname-groups of the Western Regions. Since the founding of our dynasty they have together performed their duties.

sentences.zh: 自關、隴失守，王命阻絕，忠義之徒，泣血固守，奉遵朝法，此皆侯伯守將交修共治之效，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Since Tongguan and Long were lost, royal commands blocked — men of loyalty and righteousness, weeping blood held fast, respectfully followed court law — this all the effect of marquises, earls, and garrison generals jointly cultivating and co-governing; I greatly commend it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Tongguan and Longyou were lost and imperial orders could no longer reach them, loyal men held their posts through tears and blood, still observing the laws of the court. This is the fruit of marquises, earls, and garrison commanders governing together in mutual support. I commend them deeply.

sentences.zh: 令忠可北廷大都護、四鎮節度留後，賜氏李，更名元忠。

translations.literal: Lingzhong may be Beiting Supreme Protector, Rear Commissioner of Four Garrisons military commission; granted surname Li, renamed Yuanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Lingzhong is hereby confirmed as Supreme Protector of Beiting and Rear Commissioner of the Four Garrisons, granted the imperial surname Li, and renamed Yuanzhong.

sentences.zh: 昕可安西大都護、四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: Xin may be Anxi Supreme Protector, Four Garrisons Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xin is hereby confirmed as Supreme Protector of Anxi and Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 諸將吏超七資敘官」雲。

translations.literal: All generals and officials promoted exceeding seven ranks in appointment" — so it ran.
translations.idiomatic: All generals and officials are to be promoted by more than seven ranks in seniority." Thus the edict concluded.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天寶末，盜發幽陵，外阻內訌。

translations.literal: Encomium says: At end of Tianbao, bandits rose from Youling — external obstruction, internal strife.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: At the end of the Tianbao era, rebellion broke out from Youling; the empire faced foreign enemies abroad and strife within.

sentences.zh: 子儀自朔方提孤軍，轉戰逐北，誼不還顧。

translations.literal: Ziyi from Shuofang raised a lone army, turning battle pursuing north — righteousness without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi raised a lone army from Shuofang and fought his way north without once turning back.

sentences.zh: 當是時，天子西走，唐祚若贅斿，而能輔太子，再造王室。

translations.literal: At that time, Son of Heaven fled west — Tang fortune like a surplus tassel — yet able to assist the Heir Apparent, recreate the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor fled west, and the Tang dynasty hung by a thread, yet Ziyi was able to support the heir apparent and restore the royal house.

sentences.zh: 及大難略平，遭讒甚，詭奪兵柄，然朝聞命，夕引道，無纖介自嫌。

translations.literal: When great calamity was roughly pacified, suffered slander greatly, duplicitously stripped of military power — yet morning heard command, evening set out on the road, without slightest self-complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When the great crisis had largely passed, he suffered severe slander and was cunningly stripped of military authority, yet whenever he heard an order in the morning he set out the same evening, without the slightest resentment.

sentences.zh: 及被圍涇陽，單騎見虜，壓以至誠，猜忍沮謀。

translations.literal: When besieged at Jingyang, single horse saw the barbarians — pressed with utmost sincerity, suspicion and cruelty thwarted their plots.
translations.idiomatic: When besieged at Jingyang, he rode out alone to meet the enemy and overwhelmed them with sincerity, breaking through their suspicion and cruelty to thwart their designs.

sentences.zh: 雖唐命方永，亦由忠貫日月，神明扶持者哉！

translations.literal: Although Tang mandate was then enduring — also because loyalty pierced sun and moon, spirits supported him!
translations.idiomatic: Though the Tang mandate was then enduring, it was also because his loyalty shone through sun and moon, as if sustained by the spirits themselves!

sentences.zh: 及光弼等畏偪不終，而子儀完名高節，爛然獨著，福祿永終，雖齊桓、晉文比之為褊。

translations.literal: As for Guangbi and others who feared pressure and did not finish — yet Ziyi completed name and lofty integrity, blazing alone outstanding, fortune and emolument lasting to the end — though compared to Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin would be narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Whereas men like Li Guangbi, fearing pressure, did not finish well, Guo Ziyi preserved his name and lofty integrity, shining alone in splendor, with fortune and honors lasting to the end — even compared with Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin, others seem narrow by contrast.

sentences.zh: 唐史臣裴垍稱：「權傾天下而朝不忌，功蓋一世而上不疑，侈窮人欲而議者不之貶。」

translations.literal: Tang historian Pei Ba said: "Power leaned over all under Heaven yet court did not envy; merit capped one age yet sovereign did not suspect; extravagance exhausted human desire yet critics did not demean."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang historian Pei Ba wrote: "His power leaned over the empire yet the court did not resent him; his merit capped a generation yet the sovereign did not doubt him; his extravagance exhausted every human desire yet critics did not demean him."

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 垍誠知言。

translations.literal: Ji truly knew how to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji's words were indeed apt.

sentences.zh: 其子孫多以功名顯，蓋盛德後雲。

translations.literal: His descendants for the most part achieved distinction through merit and fame — surely the aftermath of abundant virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his descendants won distinction through achievement and office — such is the legacy of great virtue.
